1.1: The Lord spake again unto Moses in the wilderness of Sinai, in the Tabernacle of the Congregation, in the first day of the second moneth, in the second yere after they were come out of the land of Egypt, saying,
1.2: Take ye the summe of all the Congregation of the children of Israel, after their families, and housholdes of their fathers with the nomber of their names: to wit, all the males, man by man:
1.3: From twentie yere old and above, all that go forth to the war in Israel, thou and Aaron shall number them, throughout their armies.
1.4: And with you shalbe men of every tribe, such as are the heads of the house of their fathers.
1.5: And these are the names of the men that shall stand with you, of the tribe of Reuben, Elizur, the sonne of Shedeur:
1.6: Of Simeon, Shelumiel the sonne of Zurishaddai:
1.7: Of Judah, Nahshon the sonne of Amminadab:
1.8: Of Issachar, Nethaneel, the sonne of Zuar:
1.9: Of Zebulun, Eliab, the sonne of Helon:
1.10: Of the children of Joseph: of Ephraim, Elishama the sonne of Ammihud: of Manasseh, Gamliel, the sonne of Pedahzur:
1.11: Of Beiamin, Abida the sonne of Gideoni:
1.12: Of Dan, Ahiezer, the sonne of Ammishaddai:
1.13: Of Asher, Pagiel, the sonne of Ocran:
1.14: Of Gad, Eliasaph, the sonne of Deuel:
1.15: Of Naphtali, Ahira the sonne of Enan.
1.16: These were famous in the Congregation, princes of the tribes of their fathers, and heads over thousands in Israel.
1.17: The Moses and Aaron took these men which are expressed by their names.
1.18: And they called all the Congregation together, in the first day of the second moneth, who declared their kindreds by their families, and by the houses of their fathers, according to the nomber of their names, from twentie yere old and above, man by man.
1.19: As the Lord had commanded Moses, so he nombred them in the wilderness of Sinai.
1.20: So were the sonnes of Reuben Israels eldest sonne by their generations, by their families, and by the houses of their fathers, according to the nomber of their names, man by man every male from twentie yere old and above, as many as went forth to war:
1.21: The nomber of them, I say, of the tribe of Reuben, was six and fourtie thousand, and five hundreth.
1.22: Of the sonnes of Simeon by their generatios, by their families, and by the houses of their fathers, the summe therof by the nomber of their names, man by man, every male from twentie yeere old and above, all that went forth to war:
1.23: The summe of them, I say, of the tribe of Simeon was nine and fiftie thousand, and three hundreth.
1.24: Of the sonnes of Gad by their generations, by their families, and by the houses of their fathers, according to the nomber of their names, from twentie yere old and above, all that went forth to war:
1.25: The number of them, I say, of the tribe of Gad was five and fourtie thousand, and six hundreth and fiftie.
1.26: Of the sonnes of Judah by their generations, by their families, and by the houses of their fathers, according to the nomber of their names, from twentie yere old and above, all that went forth to war:
1.27: The nomber of them, I say, of the tribe of Judah was three score and fourteen thousand, and six hundreth.
1.28: Of the sonnes of Issachar by their generations, by their families, and by the houses of their fathers, according to the nomber of their names, from twentie yeere old and above, all that went forth to war:
1.29: The nomber of them also of the tribe of Issachar was four and fiftie thousand and four hundreth.
1.30: Of the sonnes of Zebulun by their generations, by their families, and by the houses of their fathers, according to the number of their names, from twentie yeere old and above, all that went foorth to war:
1.31: The nomber of them also of the tribe of Zebulun was seven and fiftie thousand and four hundreth.
1.32: Of the sonnes of Joseph, namely of the sonnes of Ephraim by their generations, by their families, and by the houses of their fathers, according to the nomber of their names, from twentie yeere old and above, all that went foorth to war:
1.33: The nomber of them also of the tribe of Ephraim was fourtie thousand and five hundreth.
1.34: Of the sonnes of Manasseh by their generations, by their families, and by the houses of their fathers, according to the nomber of their names, from twentie yeere old and above, all that went foorth to war:
1.35: The nober of the also of ye tribe of Manasseh was two and thirtie thousand and two hundreth.
1.36: Of the sonnes of Beniamin by their generations, by their families, and by the houses of their fathers, according to the nomber of their names, from twentie yeere old and above, all that went foorth to war:
1.37: The nomber of them also of the tribe of Beniamin was five and thirtie thousand and four hundreth.
1.38: Of the sonnes of Dan by their generations, by their families, and by the houses of their fathers, according to the nomber of their names, from twentie yeere old and above, all that went foorth to war:
1.39: The nomber of the also of ye tribe of Dan was three score and two thousand and seue hudreth.
1.40: Of the sonnes of Asher by their generations, by their families, and by the houses of their fathers, according to the number of their names, from twentie yeere old and above, all that went foorth to war:
1.41: The nomber of them also of ye tribe of Asher was one and fourtie thousand and five hudreth.
1.42: Of the children of Naphtali, by their generations, by their families, and by the houses of their fathers, according to the nomber of their names, from twentie yeere old and above, all that went to the war:
1.43: The nomber of them also of the tribe of Naphtali, was three and fiftie thousand, and four hundreth.
1.44: These are the summes which Moses, and Aaron nombred, and the Princes of Israel, the twelve men, which were every one for the house of their fathers.
1.45: So this was all the summe of the sonnes of Israel, by the houses of their fathers, from twenty yeere old and above, all that went to the war in Israel,
1.46: And all they were in nomber six hudreth and three thousand, five hundreth and fiftie.
1.47: But the Levites, after the tribes of their fathers were not nombred among them.
1.48: For the Lord had spoken unto Moses, and said,
1.49: Onely thou shalt not number the tribe of Levi, neither take the summe of them among the children of Israel:
1.50: But thou shalt appoynt the Levites over the Tabernacle of the Testimonie, and over all the instruments thereof, and over all things that belong to it: they shall bear the Tabernacle, and all the instruments thereof, and shall minister in it, and shall dwell round about the Tabernacle.
1.51: And when the Tabernacle goeth forth, the Levites shall take it down: and when the Tabernacle is to be pitched, ye Levites shall set it up: for the stranger that cometh neere, shalbe slain.
1.52: Also the children of Israel shall pitch their tentes, every man in his camp, and every man under his standerd throughout their armies.
1.53: But the Levites shall pitch round about the Tabernacle of the Testimonie, least vengeance come upon the Congregation of the children of Israel, and the Levites shall take the charge of the Tabernacle of the Testimonie.
1.54: So the children of Israel did according to all that ye Lord had comanded Moses: so did they.

2.1: And the Lord spake unto Moses, and to Aaron, saying,
2.2: Every man of the children of Israel shall camp by his standerd, and under the ensign of their fathers house: far off about the Tabernacle of the Congregation shall they pitch.
2.3: On the East side toward the rising of the sunne, shall they of the standerd of the host of Judah pitch according to their armies: and Nahshon the sonne of Amminadab shalbe captain of the sonnes of Judah.
2.4: And his host and the nomber of the were seuentie and four thousand and six hundreth.
2.5: Next unto him shall they of the tribe of Issachar pitch, and Nethaneel the sonne of Zuar shalbe the captain of the sonnes of Issachar:
2.6: And his host, and the nomber thereof were four and fiftie thousand, and four hundreth.
2.7: Then the tribe of Zebulun, and Eliab the sonne of Helon, captain over the sonnes of Zebulun:
2.8: And his host, and the nomber thereof seven and fiftie thousand and four hundreth:
2.9: The whole nomber of the host of Judah are an hundreth fourescore and six thousand, and four hundreth according to their armies: they shall first set foorth.
2.10: On the South side shalbe ye standerd of the host of Reuben according to their armies, and the captain over the sonnes of Reuben shalbe Elizur the sonne of Shedeur.
2.11: And his host, and the nomber thereof six and fourty thousand and five hundreth.
2.12: And by him shall the tribe of Simeon pitch, and the captaiue over the sonnes of Simeon shall be Shelumiel the sonne of Zurishaddai:
2.13: And his host, and the nomber of them, nine and fiftie thousand and three hundreth.
2.14: And the tribe of Gad, and the captain over the sonnes of Gad shall be Eliasaph the sonne of Deuel:
2.15: And his host and the nomber of the were five and fourtye thousand, six hundreth and fiftie.
2.16: All the nomber of the camp of Reuben were an hundreth and one and fiftie thousand, and four hundreth and fiftie according to their armies, and they shall set foorth in the second place.
2.17: Then the Tabernacle of the Congregation shall goe with the host of the Levites, in the mids of the camp as they have pitched, so shall they goe forward, every man in his order according to their standerds.
2.18: The standerd of the camp of Ephraim shalbe toward the west according to their armies: and ye captain over the sonnes of Ephraim shall be Elishama the sonne of Ammihud:
2.19: And his host and the nomber of the were fortie thousand and five hundreth.
2.20: And by him shalbe the tribe of Manasseh, and the captain over the sonnes of Manasseh shalbe Gamliel the sonne of Pedahzur:
2.21: And his host and the nomber of them were two and thirtie thousand and two hundreth.
2.22: And the tribe of Beniamin, and ye captain over the sonnes of Beniamin shalbe Abidan the sonne of Gideoni:
2.23: And his host, and the nomber of the were five and thirtie thousand and four hundreth.
2.24: All the nomber of the camp of Ephraim were an hundreth and eight thousand and one hundreth according to their armies, and they shall go in the third place.
2.25: The standerd of the host of Dan shalbe toward the North according to their armies: and the captain over the children of Dan shall be Ahiezer the sonne of Ammishaddai:
2.26: And his host and the number of them were two and threescore thousand and seue hundreth.
2.27: And by him shall the tribe of Asher pitch, and the captain over the sonnes of Asher shalbe Pagiel the sonne of Ocran.
2.28: And his host and the nomber of them were one and fourtie thousand and five hundreth.
2.29: Then the tribe of Naphtali, and the captain over the children of Naphtali shall be Ahira the sonne of Enan:
2.30: And his host and the nomber of them were three and fiftie thousand and four hundreth.
2.31: All the nomber of the host of Dan was an hundreth and seven and fiftie thousand and six hundreth: they shall goe hinmost with their standerdes.
2.32: These are the summes of the childre of Israel by ye houses of their fathers, all the nomber of ye host, according to their armies, six hundreth and three thousand, five hundreth and fiftie.
2.33: But the Levites were not nombred among the children of Israel, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
2.34: And the children of Israel did according to all that the Lord had commanded Moses: so they pitched according to their standards, and so they journeyed every one with his families, according to the houses of their fathers.

3.1: These also were the generations of Aaron and Moses, in the day that the Lord spake with Moses in mount Sinai.
3.2: So these are the names of the sonnes of Aaron, Nadab the first borne, and Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
3.3: These are the names of the sonnes of Aaron the anoynted Priests, whom Moses did consecrate to minister in the Priests office.
3.4: And Nadab and Abihu died before the Lord, when they offred strange fire before the Lord in the wilderness of Sinai, and had no children: but Eleazar and Ithamar served in ye Priestes office in the sight of Aaron their father.
3.5: Then the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
3.6: Bring the tribe of Levi, and set the before Aaron the Priest that they may serve him,
3.7: And take the charge with him, even the charge of the whole Congregation before the Tabernacle of the Congregation to doe the service of the Tabernacle.
3.8: They shall also keep all the instruments of the Tabernacle of the Congregation, and have the charge of the children of Israel to doe the service of the Tabernacle.
3.9: And thou shalt give the Levites unto Aaron and to his sonnes: for they are given him freely from among the children of Israel.
3.10: And thou shalt appoint Aaron and his sonnes to execute their Priestes office: and the stranger that cometh neere, shalbe slayne.
3.11: Also the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
3.12: Behold, I have even taken the Levites from among the childre of Israel: for al the first borne that openeth the matrice among the children of Israel, and the Levites shalbe mine,
3.13: Because all the first borne are mine: for the same day, that I smote all the first borne in the land of Egypt, I sanctified unto me all the first borne in Israel, both man and beast: mine they shalbe: I am the Lord.
3.14: Moreover, the Lord spake unto Moses in the wilderness of Sinai, saying,
3.15: Nomber the children of Levi after the houses of their fathers, in their families: every male from a moneth old and above shalt thou nomber.
3.16: Then Moses nombred them according to the word of the Lord, as he was commanded.
3.17: And these are the sonnes of Levi by their names, Gershon, and Kohath, and Merari.
3.18: Also these are the names of the sonnes of Gershon by their families: Libni and Shimei.
3.19: The sonnes also of Kohath by their families: Amram, and Izehar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
3.20: And the sonnes of Merari by their families: Mahli and Mushi. These are the families of Levi, according to the houses of their fathers.
3.21: Of Gershon came the familie of the Libnites, and the familie of the Shimeites: these are the families of the Gershonites.
3.22: The summe whereof (after the nomber of all the males from a moneth old and above) was counted seven thousand and five hundreth.
3.23: The families of the Gershonites shall pitch behind the Tabernacle westward.
3.24: The captain and auncient of the house of the Gershonites shalbe Eliasaph the sonne of Lael.
3.25: And the charge of the sonnes of Gershon in the Tabernacle of the Congregation shall be the Tabernacle, and the pavilion, the covering thereof, and the vail of the door of the Tabernacle of the Congregation,
3.26: And the hanging of the court, and the vail of the door of the court, which is neere the Tabernacle, and neere ye Altar round about, and the cordes of it for all the service thereof.
3.27: And of Kohath came the familie of the Amramites, and the familie of the Izeharites, and the familie of the Hebronites, and the familie of the Uzzielites: these are the families of the Kohathites.
3.28: The nomber of all the males from a moneth old and above was eight thousand and six hundreth, having the charge of the Sanctuarie.
3.29: The families of the sonnes of Kohath shall pitch on the Southside of the Tabernacle.
3.30: The captain and auncient of the house, and families of the Kohathites shall be Elizaphan the sonne of Uzziel:
3.31: And their charge shalbe the Ark, and the Table, and the Candlestick, and the altars, and the instruments of the Sanctuarie that they minister with, and the vail, and all that serveth thereto.
3.32: And Eleazar the sonne of Aaron the Priest shalbe chief captain of the Levites, having the oversight of them that have the charge of the Sanctuarie.
3.33: Of Merari came the familie of the Mahlites, and the familie of the Mushites: these are the families of Merari.
3.34: And the summe of them, according to the nomber of all the males, from a moneth old and above was six thousand and two hundreth.
3.35: The captain and the ancient of the house of the families of Merari shalbe Zuriel the sonne of Abihail: they shall pitch on the Northside of the Tabernacle.
3.36: And in ye charge and custodie of the sonnes of Merari shall be the boardes of the Tabernacle, and the barres thereof, and his pillars, and his sockets, and al the instruments therof, and al that serveth thereto,
3.37: With the pillars of the court round about, with their sockets, and their pins and their coardes.
3.38: Also on the forefront of the Tabernacle toward the East, before the Tabernacle, I say, of the Congregation Eastward shall Moses and Aaron and his sonnes pitch, having the charge of the Sanctuarie, and the charge of the children of Israel: but the stranger that cometh neere, shall be slayne.
3.39: The wholesumme of ye Levites, which Moses and Aaron nombred at the commandement of the Lord throughout their families, even al the males from a moneth old and above, was two and twentie thousand.
3.40: And the Lord said unto Moses, Nomber all the first borne that are Males among the children of Israel, from a moneth old and above, and take the nomber of their names.
3.41: And thou shalt take ye Levites to me for all the first borne of the children of Israel (I am the Lord) and the cattell of the Levites for all the first borne of the cattell of the children of Israel.
3.42: And Moses nombred, as the Lord commanded him, all the first borne of the children of Israel.
3.43: And all the first borne males rehearsed by name (from a moneth old and above) according to their nomber were two and twentie thousand, two hundreth seuentie and three.
3.44: And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
3.45: Take the Levites for all the first borne of the children of Israel, and the cattell of the Levites for their cattel, and the Levites shalbe mine, (I am the Lord)
3.46: And for the redeeming of the two hundreth seuentie and three, (which are moe then the Levites) of the first borne of the children of of Israel,
3.47: Thou shalt also take five shekels for every person: after the weight of the Sanctuarie shalt thou take it: ye shekel conteineth twenty gerahs.
3.48: And thou shalt give the money, wherwith the odd nomber of them is redeemed, unto Aaron and to his sonnes.
3.49: Thus Moses took the redemption of the that were redeemed, being more then the Levites:
3.50: Of the first borne of the children of Israel took he the mony: eve a thousand three hundreth three score and five shekels after the shekel of the Sanctuarie.
3.51: And Moses gave the money of them that were redeemed, unto Aaron and to his sonnes according to the word of the Lord, as the Lord had commanded Moses.

4.1: And the Lord spake unto Moses, and to Aaron, saying,
4.2: Take the summe of the sonnes of Kohath from among the sonnes of Levi, after their families, and houses of their fathers,
4.3: From thirtie yeere old and above, even until fiftie yeere old, all that enter into the assemblie to do the work in the Tabernacle of the Congregation.
4.4: This shall be the office of the sonnes of Kohath in the Tabernacle of the Congregation about the Holiest of all.
4.5: When the host removeth, then Aaron and his sonnes shall come and take down the covering vail, and shall cover the Ark of the Testimonie therewith.
4.6: And they shall put thereon a covering of badgers skinnes, and shall spread upon it a cloth altogether of blew silk, and put to the barres thereof:
4.7: And upon ye table of shew bread they shall spread a cloth of blew silk, and put thereon the dishes, and the incense cups, and goblets, and coverings to cover it with, and the bread shall be thereon continually:
4.8: And they shall spread upon them a covering of skarlet, and cover the same with a covering of badgers skinnes, and put to the barres thereof.
4.9: Then they shall take a cloth of blew silk, and cover the candlestick of light with his lampes and his snuffers, and his snuffedishes, and al the oyle vessels thereof, which they occupie about it.
4.10: So they shall put it, and all the instruments thereof in a covering of badgers skinnes, and put it upon the barres.
4.11: Also upon the golden altar they shall spread a cloth of blew silk, and cover it with a covering of badgers skinnes, and put to the barres thereof.
4.12: And they shall take all the instruments of the ministerie wherewith they minister in the Sanctuarie, and put them in a cloth of blew silk, and cover the with a covering of badgers skinnes, and put them on the barres.
4.13: Also they shall take away the ashes from the altar, and spread a purple cloth upon it,
4.14: And shall put upon it all the instruments thereof, which they occupie about it: the censers, the fleshhookes and the besomes, and the basens, even al the instruments of the altar and they shall spread upon it a covering of badgers skinnes, and put to the barres of it.
4.15: And when Aaron and his sonnes have made an end of covering the Sanctuarie, and al the instruments of the Sanctuarie, at the removing of the host, afterward the sonnes of Kohath shall come to bear it, but they shall not touch any holy thing, lest they dye. This is the charge of the sonnes of Kohath in the Tabernacle of the Congregation.
4.16: And to the office of Eleazar the sonne of Aaron the Priest pertaineth the oyle for the light, and the sweet incense and the dayly meat offring, and the anointing oyle, with the oversight of all the Tabernacle, and of all that therein is, both in the Sanctuarie and in all the instruments thereof.
4.17: And the Lord spake unto Moses and to Aaron, saying,
4.18: Ye shall not cut off the tribe of the families of the Kohathites from among the Levites:
4.19: But thus do unto them, that they may live and not die, when they come neere to the most holy things: let Aaron and his sonnes come and appoynt them, every one to his office, and to his charge.
4.20: But let them not goe in, to see when the Sanctuarie is folden up, lest they die.
4.21: And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
4.22: Take also ye summe of the sonnes of Gershon, every one by the houses of their fathers throughout their families:
4.23: From thirtie yere old and above, until fiftie yere old shalt thou nomber them, al that enter into the assemblie for to do service in the Tabernacle of the Congregation.
4.24: This shall be the service of the families of the Gershonites, to serve and to bear.
4.25: They shall bear the curtaines of the Tabernacle, and the Tabernacle of the Congregation, his covering, and the covering of badgers skinnes, that is on hie upon it, and the vayle of the door of the Tabernacle of the Congregation:
4.26: The curtaines also of the court, and the vail of the entring in of the gate of the court, which is neere the Tabernacle and neere the altar round about, with their cordes, and all the instruments for their service, and all that is made for them: so shall they serve.
4.27: At the commandement of Aaron and his sonnes shall all the service of the sonnes of ye Gershonites bee done, in all their charges and in all their service, and ye shall appoynt them to keep all their charges.
4.28: This is the service of the families of the sonnes of the Gershonites in the Tabernacle of the Congregation, and their watch shall be under the hand of Ithamar the sonne of Aaron the Priest.
4.29: Thou shalt nomber the sonnes of Merari by their families, and by the houses of their fathers:
4.30: From thirty yere old and above, even unto fiftie yere old shalt thou nomber the, all that enter into the assemblie, to doe the service of the Tabernacle of the Congregation.
4.31: And this is their office and charge according to all their service in the Tabernacle of the Congregation: the boardes of the Tabernacle with the barres thereof, and his pillars, and his sockets,
4.32: And the pillars round about the court, with their sockets and their pinnes, and their cords, with all their instruments, even for all their service: and by name ye shall recken the instruments of their office and charge.
4.33: This is the service of the families of the sonnes of Merari, according to all their service in the Tabernacle of the Congregation under the hand of Ithamar the sonne of Aaron the Priest.
4.34: Then Moses and Aaron and the princes of the Congregation nombred the sonnes of the Kohathites, by their families and by the houses of their fathers,
4.35: From thirtie yeere old and above, even unto fiftie yere old, all that enter into the assemblie for the service of the Tabernacle of ye Congregation.
4.36: So the nombers of the throughout their families were two thousand, seven hundreth and fiftie.
4.37: These are the nombers of the families of the Kohathites, al that serve in the Tabernacle of the Congregation, which Moses and Aaron did nomber according to the commandement of the Lord by the hand of Moses.
4.38: Also the nombers of the sonnes of Gershon throughout their families and houses of their fathers,
4.39: From thirtie yere old and vpwarde, even unto fiftie yere old: all that enter into the assemblie for the service of the Tabernacle of the Cogregation.
4.40: So the nombers of them by their families, and by the houses of their fathers were two thousand six hundreth and thirtie.
4.41: These are the nombers of the families of the sonnes of Gershon: of all that did service in the Tabernacle of the Congregation, whom Moses and Aaron did nomber according to the commandement of the Lord.
4.42: The nombers also of the families of the sonnes of Merari by their families, and by the houses of their fathers,
4.43: From thirtie yeere old and vpwarde, even unto fiftie yeere old: all that enter into the assemblie for the service of the Tabernacle of the Congregation.
4.44: So the nombers of them by their families were three thousand, and two hundreth.
4.45: These are the summes of ye families of the sonnes of Merari, whom Moses and Aaron nombred according to the commandement of the Lord, by the hand of Moses.
4.46: So all the nombers of the Levites, which Moses, and Aaron, and the princes of Israel nombred by their families and by the houses of their fathers,
4.47: From thirtie yere old and upward, even to fiftie yeere old, every one that came to doe his duetie, office, service and charge in the Tabernacle of the Congregation.
4.48: So the nombers of them were eight thousand, five hundreth and four score.
4.49: According to the commandement of the Lord by the hand of Moses did Aaron nomber them, every one according to his service, and according to his charge. Thus were they of that tribe nombred, as the Lord commanded Moses.

5.1: And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
5.2: Commaund the children of Israel that they put out of the host every leper, and every one that hath an issue, and whosoever is defiled by the dead.
5.3: Both male and female shall ye put out: out of the host shall yee put them, that they defile not their tentes among whom I dwell.
5.4: And the children of Israel did so, and put them out of the host, even as the Lord had commanded Moses, so did the children of Israel.
5.5: And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
5.6: Speak unto the children of Israel, When a man or woman shall commit any sinne that men commit, and transgress against the Lord, when that person shall trespass,
5.7: Then they shall confess their sinne which they have done, and shall restore the domage thereof with his principal, and put the fift part of it more thereto, and shall give it unto him, against whom he hath trespassed.
5.8: But if the man have no kinseman, to whom he should restore the domage, the domage shall be restored to the Lord for the Priests use besides the ramme of the atonement, whereby hee shall make atonement for him.
5.9: And every offring of all the holy thinges of the children of Israel, which they bring unto the Priest, shalbe his.
5.10: And every mans halowed things shall bee his: that is, whatsoever any man giveth the Priest, it shalbe his.
5.11: And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
5.12: Speak unto the children of Israel, and say unto them, If any mans wife turn to evil, and commit a trespass against him,
5.13: So that an other man lie with her fleshly, and it bee hid from the eyes of her husband, and kept close, and yet she be defiled, and there be no witness against her, neither she taken with the maner,
5.14: If he be moved with a ielous mind, so that he is ielous over his wife, which is defiled, or if he have a ielous mind, so that he is ielous over his wife, which is not defiled,
5.15: Then shall the man bring his wife to the Priest, and bring her offering with her, the tenth part of an Ephah of barly meal, but he shall not powre oyle upon it, nor put incense thereon: for it is an offring of ielousie, an offring for a remembrance, calling the sinne to mind:
5.16: And the Priest shall bring her, and set her before the Lord.
5.17: Then the Priest shall take the holy water in an earthen vessel, and of the dust that is in the floor of the Tabernacle, even the Priest shall take it and put it into the water.
5.18: After, the Priest shall set the woman before the Lord, and vncouer the womans head, and put the offring of the memorial in her hands: it is the ielousie offering, and the Priest shall have bitter and cursed water in his hand,
5.19: And the Priest shall charge her by an othe, and say unto the woman, If no man have lien with thee, neither thou hast turned to vncleannesse from thine husband, be free from this bitter and cursed water.
5.20: But if thou hast turned from thine husband, and so art defiled, and some man hath lyen with thee beside thine husband,
5.21: (Then the Priest shall charge the woman with an othe of cursing, and the Priest shall say unto the woman) The Lord make thee to be accursed, and detestable for the othe among thy people, and the Lord cause thy thigh to rot, and thy belly to swell:
5.22: And that this cursed water may goe into thy bowels, to cause thy belly to swell, and thy thigh to rot. Then the woman shall answer, Amen, Amen.
5.23: After, the Priest shall write these curses in a book, and shall blot them out with the bitter water,
5.24: And shall cause the woman to drink ye bitter and cursed water, and the cursed water, turned into bitterness, shall enter into her.
5.25: Then the Priest shall take the ielousie offring out of the womans hand, and shall shake the offring before the Lord, and offer it upon ye altar.
5.26: And the Priest shall take an handful of the offring for a memorial thereof, and burn it upon the altar, and afterward make the woman drink the water.
5.27: When yee have made her drink the water, (if she bee defiled and have trespassed against her husband) then shall the cursed water, turned into bitterness, enter into her, and her belly shall swell, and her thigh shall rot, and the woman shall be accursed among her people.
5.28: But if the woman bee not defiled, but bee clean, she shalbe free and shall conceive and bear.
5.29: This is the law of ielousie, when a wife turneth from her husband and is defiled,
5.30: Or when a man is moved with a ielous mind being ielous over his wife then shall he bring the woman before the Lord, and the Priest shall do to her according to al this law,
5.31: And the man shalbe free from sinne, but this woman shall bear her iniquitie.

6.1: And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
6.2: Speak unto the children of Israel, and say unto them, When a man or a woman doeth separate themselves to vow a vow of a Nazarite to separate himself unto the Lord,
6.3: He shall abstain from wine and strong drink, and shall drink no sowre wine nor sowre drink, nor shall drink any licour of grapes, neither shall eat fresh grapes nor dryed.
6.4: As long as his abstinence endureth, shall hee eat nothing that is made of the wine of the vine, neither the kernels, nor the husk.
6.5: While hee is separate by his vow, the rasor shall not come upon his head, until the dayes be out, in the which he separateth him self unto the Lord, he shalbe holy, and shall let the lockes of the hear of his head grow.
6.6: During the time that he separateth himself unto the Lord, he shall come at no dead body:
6.7: Hee shall not make himself vncleane at the death of his father, or mother, brother, or sister: for the consecration of his God is upon his head.
6.8: All the dayes of his separation he shalbe holy to the Lord.
6.9: And if any dye suddenly by him, or hee beware, then the head of his consecration shall be defiled, and he shall shave his head in the day of his clensing: in the seventh day he shall shave it.
6.10: And in the eight day hee shall bring two turtles, or two yong pigeons to the Priest, at the door of the Tabernacle of the Congregation.
6.11: Then the Priest shall prepare the one for a sinne offering, and the other for a burnt offering, and shall make an atonement for him, because he sinned by the dead: so shall he halowe his head the same day,
6.12: And he shall consecrate unto the Lord the dayes of his separation, and shall bring a lamb of a yeere old for a trespass offering, and the first dayes shalbe void: for his consecration was defiled.
6.13: This then is the law of the Nazarite: When the time of his consecration is out, he shall come to the door of the Tabernacle of the Congregation,
6.14: And hee shall bring his offering unto the Lord, an hee lamb of a yeere old without blemish for a burnt offering, and a she lamb of a yere old without blemish for a sinne offring, and a ramme without blemish for peace offrings,
6.15: And a basket of vnleauened bread, of cakes of fine flour, mingled with oyle, and wafers of vnleauened bread anointed with oil, with their meat offring, and their drink offrings:
6.16: The which the Priest shall bring before the Lord, and make his sinne offering and his burnt offering.
6.17: He shall prepare also the ram for a peace offring unto the Lord, with the basket of vnleauened bread, and the Priest shall make his meat offring, and his drink offring.
6.18: And the Nazarite shall shave the head of his consecration at the door of the Tabernacle of the Congregation, and shall take the hear of the head of his consecration, and put it in the fire, which is under the peace offring.
6.19: Then the Priest shall take ye sodden shoulder of the ramme, and an vnleauened cake out of the basket, and a wafer vnleauened, and put them upon the hands of the Nazarite, after he hath shaven his consecration.
6.20: And the Priest shall shake them to and from before the Lord: this is an holy thing for the Priest besides the shaken breast, and besides the heave shoulder: so afterward the Nazarite may drink wine.
6.21: This is the Law of the Nazarite, which he hath vowed, and of his offering unto the Lord for his consecration, besides that that hee is able to bring: according to the vow which he vowed, so shall he do after the law of his consecration.
6.22: And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
6.23: Speak unto Aaron and to his sonnes, saying, Thus shall ye bless the childre of Israel, and say unto them,
6.24: The Lord bless thee, and keep thee,
6.25: The Lord make his face shine upon thee, and be merciful unto thee,
6.26: The Lord lift up his coutenance upon thee, and give thee peace.
6.27: So they shall put my Name upon the children of Israel, and I wil bless them.

7.1: Now when Moses had finished the setting up of the Tabernacle, and anointed it and sanctified it, and all the instruments thereof, and the altar with al the instruments thereof, and had anoynted them and sanctified them,
7.2: Then the princes of Israel, heads over the houses of their fathers (they were the princes of the tribes, who were over them that were nombred) offred,
7.3: And brought their offring before the Lord, six covered charets, and twelve oxen: one charet for two princes, and for every one an oxe, and they offred them before the Tabernacle.
7.4: And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
7.5: Take these of them, that they may be to doe the service of the Tabernacle of the Congregation, and thou shalt give them unto the Levites, to every man according unto his office.
7.6: So Moses took the charets and the oxen, and gave them unto the Levites:
7.7: Two charets and four oxen hee gave to the sonnes of Gershon, according unto their office.
7.8: And four charets and eight oxen hee gave to the sonnes of Merari according unto their office, under the hand of Ithamar the sonne of Aaron the Priest.
7.9: But to the sonnes of Kohath he gave none, because the charge of the Sanctuarie belonged to them, which they did bear upon their shoulders.
7.10: The princes also offered in the dedication for the altar in the day that it was anoynted: then the princes offered their offering before the altar.
7.11: And the Lord sayd unto Moses, One prince one day, and an other prince an other day shall offer their offring, for the dedication of the altar.
7.12: So then on the first day did Nahshon the sonne of Amminadab of ye tribe of Judah offer his offring.
7.13: And his offring was a silver charger of an hundreth and thirtie shekels weight, a silver boule of seventy shekels, after the shekel of the Sanctuarie, both ful of fine flour, mingled with oyle, for a meat offring,
7.14: An incense cup of gold of tenne shekels, ful of incense,
7.15: A yong bullock, a ram, a lamb of a yeere old for a burnt offring,
7.16: An hee goat for a sinne offring,
7.17: And for peace offrings, two bullockes, five rams, five hee goates, and five lambes of a yeere old: this was the offring of Nahshon the sonne of Amminadab.
7.18: The second day Nethaneel, the sonne of Zuar, prince of the tribe of Issachar did offer:
7.19: Who offred for his offring a silver charger of an hundreth and thirtie shekels weight, a silver boule of seuentie shekels, after the shekel of the Sanctuarie, both ful of fine flour, mingled with oyle, for a meat offring,
7.20: An incense cup of gold of ten shekels, ful of incense,
7.21: A yong bullock, a ram, a lamb of a yeere old for a burnt offring,
7.22: An hee goat for a sinne offring,
7.23: And for peace offrings, two bullockes, five rammes, five hee goates, five lambes of a yeere old: this was the offring of Nethaneel the sonne of Zuar.
7.24: The third day Eliab the sonne of Helon prince of the children of Zebulun offred.
7.25: His offring was a silver charger of an hundreth and thirty shekels weight, a silver boule of seuentie shekels, after the shekel of the Sanctuarie, both ful of fine flour, mingled with oyle, for a meat offring,
7.26: A golden incense cup of ten shekels, ful of incense,
7.27: A yong bullock, a ram, a lamb of a yeere old for a burnt offring,
7.28: An hee goat for a sinne offring,
7.29: And for peace offrings, two bullockes, five rammes, five hee goates, five lambes of a yeere old: this was the offering of Eliab the sonne of Helon.
7.30: The fourth day Elizur ye sonne of Shedeur prince of the children of Reuben offred.
7.31: His offring was a silver charger of an hundreth and thirtie shekels weight, a silver boule of seuentie shekels, after the shekel of the Sanctuary, both ful of fine flour, mingled with oyle, for a meat offring,
7.32: A golden incense cup of ten shekels, full of incense,
7.33: A yong bullock, a ram, a lamb of a yere old for a burnt offring,
7.34: An hee goat for a sinne offring,
7.35: And for a peace offring, two bullockes, five rammes, five hee goates, and five lambes of a yere old: this was the offering of Elizur the sonne of Shedeur.
7.36: The fifth day Shelumiel the sonne of Zurishaddai, prince of the children of Simeon offered.
7.37: His offring was a silver charger of an hundreth and thirtie shekels weight, a silver boule of seuentie shekels, after the shekel of the Sanctuary, both ful of fine flour, mingled with oyle, for a meat offring,
7.38: A golden incense cup of ten shekels, full of incense,
7.39: A yong bullock, a ram, a lamb of a yeere old for a burnt offring,
7.40: An hee goat for a sinne offring,
7.41: And for a peace offring, two bullocks, five rammes, five hee goates, five lambes of a yere old: this was the offering of Shelumiel the sonne of Zurishaddai.
7.42: The sixt day Eliasaph the sonne of Deuel prince of the children of Gad offred.
7.43: His offring was a silver charger of an hundreth and thirtie shekels weight, a silver boule of seuentie shekels, after the shekel of the Sanctuarie, both ful of fine flour, mingled with oyle, for a meat offring,
7.44: A golden incense cup of ten shekels, full of incense,
7.45: A yong bullock, a ram, a lamb of a yere old, for a burnt offring,
7.46: An hee goat for a sinne offring,
7.47: And for a peace offering, two bullockes, five rammes, five hee goates, five lambes of a yere old: this was the offring of Eliasaph the sonne of Deuel.
7.48: The seventh day Elishama the sonne of Ammiud prince of the children of Ephraim offered.
7.49: His offring was a silver charger of an hundreth and thirtie shekels weight, a silver boule of seuentie shekels, after the shekel of the Sanctuary, both full of fine flour, mingled with oyle, for a meat offering,
7.50: A golden incense cup of ten shekels, full of incense,
7.51: A yong bullock, a ram, a lamb of a yeere old for a burnt offring,
7.52: An hee goat for a sinne offring,
7.53: And for a peace offring, two bullockes, five rammes, five hee goates, five lambes of a yeere old: this was the offring of Elishama the sonne of Ammiud.
7.54: The eight day offred Gamliel the sonne of Pedazur, prince of the children of Manasseh.
7.55: His offring was a silver charger of an hundreth and thirtie shekels weight, a silver boule of seuentie shekels, after the shekel of the Sanctuarie, both full of fine flour, mingled with oyle, for a meat offring,
7.56: A golden incense cup of ten shekels, full of incense,
7.57: A yong bullock, a ram, a lamb of a yeere old for a burnt offring,
7.58: An hee goat for a sinne offring,
7.59: And for a peace offring, two bullockes, five rammes, five hee goates, five lambes of a yeere old: this was the offring of Gamliel the sonne of Pedazur.
7.60: The ninth day Abidan the sonne of Gideoni prince of the children of Beniamin offered.
7.61: His offring was a silver charger of an hundreth and thirtie shekels weight, a silver boule of seuentie shekels, after the shekel of the Sanctuarie, both full of fine flour, mingled with oyle, for a meat offring,
7.62: A golden incense cup of ten shekels, full of incense,

7.65: And for a peace offring, two bullockes, five rammes, five hee goates, five lambes of a yeere old: this was the offring of Abidan the sonne of Gideoni.
7.66: The tenth day Ahiezer the sonne of Ammishaddai, prince of the children of Dan offred.
7.67: His offring was a silver charger of an hundreth and thirtie shekels weight, a silver boule of seuentie shekels, after the shekel of the Sanctuarie, both full of fine flour, mingled with oyle, for a meat offring,
7.68: A golden incense cup of ten shekels full of incense,
7.69: A yong bullock, a ram, a lamb of a yeere old for a burnt offring,
7.70: An hee goat for a sinne offring,
7.71: And for a peace offring, two bullocks, five rammes, five hee goates, five lambes of a yeere old: this was the offring of Ahiezer the sonne of Ammishaddai.
7.72: The eleventh day Pagiel the sonne of Ocran, prince of the children of Asher offred.
7.73: His offring was a silver charger of an hundreth and thirtie shekels weight, a silver boule of seuentie shekels, after the shekel of the Sanctuarie, both full of fine flour, mingled with oyle, for a meat offring,
7.74: A golden incense cup of ten shekels, ful of incense,
7.75: A yong bullock, a ram, a lamb of a yere old for a burnt offring,
7.76: An hee goat for a sinne offring,
7.77: And for a peace offring, two bullockes, five rams, five he goates, five lambes of a yeere old: this was the offring of Pagiel the sonne of Ocran.
7.78: The twelfth day Ahira the sonne of Enan, prince of the children of Naphtali offred,
7.79: His offring was a silver charger of an hundreth and thirtie shekels weight, a silver boule of seuentie shekels, after the shekel of the Sanctuarie, both full of fine flour, mingled with oyle, for a meat offring,
7.80: A golden incense cup of ten shekels, ful of incense,
7.81: A yong bullock, a ram, a lamb of a yere old for a burnt offring,
7.82: An hee goat for a sinne offring,
7.83: And for peace offerings, two bullockes, five rammes, five hee goates, five lambes of a yeere old: this was the offering of Ahira the sonne of Enan.
7.84: This was the dedication of the Altar by the princes of Israel, whe it was anointed: twelve chargers of silver, twelve silver boules, twelve incense cuppes of gold,
7.85: Every charger, conteining an hundreth and thirtie shekels of silver, and every boule seuentie: all the silver vessell conteined two thousand and four hundreth shekels, after the shekel of the Sanctuarie.
7.86: Twelve incense cups of gold ful of incense, conteining ten shekels every cup, after the shekel of the Sanctuarie: all the gold of the incense cups was an hundreth and twentie shekels.
7.87: All the bullockes for the burnt offering were twelve bullocks, the rams twelve, the lambs of a yeere old twelve, with their meat offrings, and twelve hee goates for a sinne offring.
7.88: And all the bullocks for the peace offrings were four and twentie bullockes, the rammes sixtie, the hee goates sixtie, the lambes of a yeere old sixtie: this was the dedication of the Altar, after that it was anointed.
7.89: And when Moses went into the Tabernacle of the Congregation, to speak with God, he heard the voyce of one speaking unto him from the Merciseat, that was upon the Ark of the Testimonie between the two Cherubims, and he spake to him.

8.1: And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
8.2: Speak unto Aaron, and say unto him, When thou lightest the lampes, the seven lampes shall give light toward the forefront of the Candlestick.
8.3: And Aaron did so, lighting the lampes thereof toward ye forefront of the Candlestick, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
8.4: And this was the work of the Candlestick, even of gold beaten out with the hammer, both the shaft, and the flowres thereof was beaten out with the hammer: according to the paterne, which the Lord had shewed Moses, so made he the Candlestick.
8.5: And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
8.6: Take the Levites from among the children of Israel, and purifie them.
8.7: And thus shalt thou doe unto them, when thou purifiest them, Sprinckle water of purification upon them, and let them shave all their flesh, and wash their clothes: so they shalbe clean.
8.8: Then they shall take a yong bullock with his meat offring of fine flour, mingled with oyle, and another yong bullock shalt thou take for a sinne offring.
8.9: Then thou shalt bring the Levites before the Tabernacle of the Congregation, and asseble all the Congregation of the children of Israel.
8.10: Thou shalt bring the Levites also before the Lord, and the children of Israel shall put their handes upon the Levites.
8.11: And Aaron shall offer the Levites before the Lord, as a shake offring of ye childre of Israel, that they may execute the service of the Lord.
8.12: And the Levites shall put their handes upon the heades of the bullockes, and make thou the one a sinne offring, and the other a burnt offring unto the Lord, that thou mayest make an atonement for the Levites.
8.13: And thou shalt set the Levites before Aaron and before his sonnes, and offer the as a shake offring to the Lord.
8.14: Thus thou shalt separate the Levites from among the children of Israel, and the Levites shall be mine.
8.15: And afterward shall the Levites goe in, to serve in the Tabernacle of the Congregation, and thou shalt purifie them and offer them, as a shake offering.
8.16: For they are freely given unto me from among the children of Israel, for such as open any womb: for all the first borne of the children of Israel have I taken them unto me.
8.17: For all the first borne of the children of Israel are mine, both of man and of beast: since the day that I smote every first borne in the land of Egypt, I sanctified them for my self.
8.18: And I have taken the Levites for all the first borne of the children of Israel,
8.19: And have given the Levites as a gift unto Aaron, and to his sonnes from among the children of Israel, to do the service of the children of Israel in the Tabernacle of the Congregation, and to make an atonement for the children of Israel, that there be no plague among the children of Israel, when the children of Israel come neere unto the Sanctuarie.
8.20: Then Moses and Aaron and all the Cogregation of the children of Israel did with the Levites, according unto all that the Lord had commanded Moses concerning the Levites: so did the children of Israel unto them.
8.21: So the Levites were purified, and washed their clothes, and Aaron offred them as a shake offring before the Lord, and Aaron made an atonement for them, to purifie them.
8.22: And after that, went the Levites in to doe their service in the Tabernacle of the Congregation, before Aaron and before his sonnes: as the Lord had commanded Moses concerning the Levites, so they did unto them.
8.23: And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
8.24: This also belongeth to the Levites: from five and twentie yeere old and vpwarde, they shall goe in, to execute their office in the service of the Tabernacle of the Congregation.
8.25: And after the age of fiftie yeere, they shall cease from executing the office, and shall serve no more:
8.26: But they shall minister with their brethre in the Tabernacle of the Congregation, to keep things committed to their charge, but they shall doe no service: thus shalt thou doe unto the Levites touching their charges.

9.1: And the Lord spake unto Moses in the wildernes of Sinai, in the first moneth of the second yeere, after they were come out of the land of Egypt, saying,
9.2: The children of Israel shall also celebrate the Passeouer at ye time appointed thereunto.
9.3: In the fourtenth day of this moneth at even, ye shall keep it in his due season: according to all the ordinances of it, and according to all the ceremonies thereof shall ye keep it.
9.4: Then Moses spake unto the children of Israel, to celebrate the Passeouer.
9.5: And they kept the Passeouer in the fouretenth day of the first moneth at even in the wilderness of Sinai: according to all that the Lord had comanded Moses, so did ye children of Israel.
9.6: And certain men were defiled by a dead man, that they might not keep the Passeouer the same day: and they came before Moses and before Aaron the same day.
9.7: And those men said unto him, We are defiled by a dead man: wherefore are wee kept back that we may not offer an offering unto the Lord in the time thereunto appointed among the children of Israel?
9.8: Then Moses said unto them, Stand still, and I will hear what the Lord will command concerning you.
9.9: And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
9.10: Speak unto the children of Israel, and say, If any amog you, or of your posteritie shalbe vncleane by ye reason of a corps, or be in a log journey, he shall keep the Passeouer unto ye Lord.
9.11: In the fourtenth day of the second moneth at even they shall keep it: with vnleauened bread and sowre herbes shall they eat it.
9.12: They shall leave none of it unto the morning, nor break any bone of it: according to all the ordinance of the Passeouer shall they keep it.
9.13: But the man that is clean and is not in a journey, and is negligent to keep the Passeouer, the same person shalbe cut off from his people: because he brought not the offring of the Lord in his due season, that man shall bear his sinne.
9.14: And if a stranger dwell among you, and wil keep the Passeouer unto the Lord, as the ordinance of the Passeouer, and as the maner thereof is, so shall he do: ye shall have one law both for the stranger, and for him that was borne in the same land.
9.15: And when the Tabernacle was reared up, a cloud covered the Tabernacle, namely the Tabernacle of the Testimonie: and at even there was upon the Tabernacle, as the appearance of fire until the morning.
9.16: So it was alway: the cloud covered it by day, and the appearance of fire by night.
9.17: And when the cloud was taken up from the Tabernacle, then afterward the children of Israel journeyed: and in the place where the cloud abode, there the children of Israel pitched their tents.
9.18: At the commandement of the Lord the children of Israel journeyed, and at the comandement of the Lord they pitched: as long as the cloud abode upon the Tabernacle, they lay still.
9.19: And when the cloud taryed stil upon the Tabernacle a long time, the childre of Israel kept the watch of the Lord, and journeyed not.
9.20: So when the cloud abode a few dayes upon the Tabernacle, they abode in their tents according to the comandement of ye Lord: for they journeyed at the commandement of the Lord.
9.21: And though the cloud abode upon the Tabernacle from even unto the morning, yet if the cloud was taken up in the morning, then they journeyed: whether by day or by night the cloud was taken up, then they journeyed.
9.22: Or if the cloud taryed two dayes or a moneth, or a yeere upon the Tabernacle, abiding thereon, the children of Israel abode still, and journeyed not: but when it was taken up, they journeyed.
9.23: At the commandement of the Lord they pitched, and at the commandement of the Lord they journeyed, keeping the watch of the Lord at the commandement of the Lord by the hand of Moses.

10.1: And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
10.2: Make thee two trumpets of silver: of an whole piece shalt thou make the, that thou mayest use them for the assembling of the Congregation, and for the departure of the camp.
10.3: And when they shall blow with them, all the Congregation shall assemble to thee before the door of the Tabernacle of the Cogregation.
10.4: But if they blow with one, then the princes, or heades over the thousandes of Israel shall come unto thee.
10.5: But if ye blow an alarm, then the camp of the that pitch on the East part, shall go forward.
10.6: If ye blow an alarm the second time, then the host of them that lie on the Southside shall march: for they shall blow an alarm when they remove.
10.7: But in assembling the Congregation, ye shall blow without an alarm.
10.8: And the sonnes of Aaron the Priest shall blow the trumpets, and ye shall have them as a law for ever in your generations.
10.9: And when ye goe to war in your land against the enemie that vexeth you, ye shall blow an alarm with the trumpets, and ye shall bee remembred before the Lord your God, and shalbe saved from your enemies.
10.10: Also in the day of your gladness, and in your feast dayes, and in the beginning of your moneths, ye shall also blow the trumpets over your burnt sacrifices, and over your peace offrings, that they may be a remembrance for you before your God: I am the Lord your God.
10.11: And in the second yeere, in the second moneth, and in the twentieth day of the moneth the cloud was taken up from the Tabernacle of the Testimonie.
10.12: And ye children of Israel departed on their journeys out of the desart of Sinai, and the cloud rested in the wilderness of Paran.
10.13: So they first took their journey at the comandement of the Lord, by ye hand of Moses.
10.14: In the first place went the standerd of the host of the children of Judah, according to their armies: and Nahshon the sonne of Amminabad was over his band.
10.15: And over the band of the tribe of the children of Issachar was Nethaneel ye sonne of Zuar.
10.16: And over the band of the tribe of the children of Zebulun was Eliab the sonne of Helon.
10.17: When the Tabernacle was taken down, then the sonnes of Gershon, and the sonnes of Merari went forward bearing the Tabernacle.
10.18: After, departed the standerd of the host of Reuben, according to their armies, and over his band was Elizur the sonne of Shedeur.
10.19: And over the band of the tribe of ye children of Simeon was Shelumiel the sonne of Shurishaddai.
10.20: And over the band of the tribe of ye children of Gad was Eliasaph the sonne of Deuel.
10.21: The Kohathites also went forward and bare the Sanctuarie, and the former did set up the Tabernacle against they came.
10.22: Then the standerd of the host of the children of Ephraim went forward according to their armies, and over his band was Elishama the sonne of Ammiud.
10.23: And over the band of the tribe of ye sonnes of Manasseh was Gamliel the sonne of Pedazur.
10.24: And over the band of ye tribe of the sonnes of Beniamin was Abidan the sonne of Gideoni.
10.25: Last, the standerd of the host of the children of Dan marched, gathering all ye hostes according to their armies: and over his band was Ahiezer the sonne of Ammishaddai.
10.26: And over the band of the tribe of the children of Asher was Pagiel the sonne of Ocran.
10.27: And over the band of the tribe of the children of Naphtali was Ahira ye sonne of Enan.
10.28: These were the remouings of the children of Israel according to their armies, whe they marched.
10.29: After, Moses said unto Hobab ye sonne of Reuel the Midianite, ye father in law of Moses, We go into the place, of which ye Lord said, I will give it you: Come thou with us, and we wil doe thee good: for ye Lord hath promised good unto Israel.
10.30: And he answered him, I will not goe: but I will depart to mine own countrey, and to my kindred.
10.31: Then he sayd, I pray thee, leave us not: for thou knowest our camping places in the wilderness: therefore thou mayest be our guide.
10.32: And if thou go with us, what goodnes the Lord shall shew unto us, the same will we shew unto thee.
10.33: So they departed from the mount of the Lord, three dayes journey: and the Ark of the covenant of the Lord went before them in the three dayes journey, to search out a resting place for them.
10.34: And the cloud of the Lord was upon the by day, when they went out of the camp.
10.35: And when the Ark went forward, Moses said, Rise up, Lord, and let thine enemies bee scattered, and let them that hate thee, flee before thee.
10.36: And when it rested, hee sayde, Return, O Lord, to the many thousands of Israel.

11.1: When the people became murmurers, it displeased the Lord: and the Lord heard it, therefore his wrath was kindled, and the fire of the Lord burnt among them, and consumed the utmost part of the host.
11.2: Then the people cryed unto Moses: and when Moses praied unto the Lord, the fire was quenched.
11.3: And he called the name of that place Taberah, because the fire of the Lord burnt among them.
11.4: And a nomber of people that was amog them, fell a lusting, and turned away, and the children of Israel also wept, and said, Who shall give us flesh to eat?
11.5: We remember the fish which we did eat in Egypt for nought, the cucumbers, and the pepons, and the leekes, and the onions, and the garleke.
11.6: But now our soul is dryed away, we can see nothing but this Man.
11.7: (The Man also was as coriander seed, and his colour like the colour of bdelium.
11.8: The people went about and gathered it, and ground it in milles, or beat it in morters, and baked it in a cauldron, and made cakes of it, and the taste of it was like unto the taste of fresh oyle.
11.9: And when the dew fell down upon the host in the night, the Man fell with it)
11.10: Then Moses heard the people weep throughout their families, every man in the door of his tent, and the wrath of the Lord was grieuously kindled: also Moses was grieved.
11.11: And Moses said unto the Lord, Wherefore hast thou vexed thy servant? and why have I not found fauour in thy sight, seeing thou hast put the charge of al this people upon mee?
11.12: Have I conceived al this people? or have I begotte them, that thou shouldest say unto me, Cary them in thy bosom (as a nurse beareth the sucking child) unto the land, for the which thou swarest unto their fathers?
11.13: Where should I have flesh to give unto al this people? for they weep unto me, saying, Give us flesh that we may eat.
11.14: I am not able to bear al this people alone, for it is too heauie for me.
11.15: Therefore if thou deal thus with mee, I pray thee, if I have found fauour in thy sight, kill me, that I behold not my miserie.
11.16: Then the Lord said unto Moses, Gather unto me seuetie men of ye Elders of Israel, whom thou knowest, that they are the Elders of the people, and gouernonrs over them, and bring them unto the Tabernacle of the Congregation, and let them stand there with thee,
11.17: And I will come down, and talk with thee there, and take of the Spirit, which is upon thee, and put upon them, and they shall bear the burthen of the people with thee: so thou shalt not bear it alone.
11.18: Furthermore thou shalt say unto the people, Bee sanctified against to morowe, and yee shall eat flesh: for you have wept in the eares of the Lord, saying, Who shall give us flesh to eat? for we were better in Egypt: therefore the Lord will give you flesh, and ye shall eat.
11.19: Ye shall not eat one day nor two daies, nor five daies, neither ten daies, nor twentie dayes,
11.20: But a whole moneth, until it come out at your nostrels, and bee lothesome unto you, because ye have contemned the Lord, which is among you, and have wept before him, saying, Why came we hither out of Egypt?
11.21: And Moses said, Six hundreth thousand footemen are there of the people, among whom I am: and thou saiest, I will give them flesh, that they may eat a moneth long.
11.22: Shall the sheep and the beeves be slain for them, to find them? either shall all the fish of the sea be gathered together for them to suffice them?
11.23: And the Lord said unto Moses, Is the Lordes hand shortened? thou shalt see now whether my word shall come to pass unto thee, or no.
11.24: So Moses went out, and told the people the wordes of the Lord, and gathered seuentie men of the Elders of the people, and set them round about the Tabernacle.
11.25: Then the Lord came down in a cloud, and spake unto him, and took of the Spirit that was upon him, and put it upon the seuentie Ancient men: and when the Spirit rested upon them, then they prophecied, and did not cease.
11.26: But there remained two of the men in the host: the name of the one was Eldad, and the name of the other Medad, and the Spirit rested upon them, (for they were of them that were written, and went not out unto the Tabernacle) and they prophecied in the host.
11.27: Then there ranne a yong man, and told Moses, and said, Eldad and Medad doe prophesie in the host.
11.28: And Joshua the sonne of Nun the servant of Moses one of his yong men answered and said, My lord Moses, forbid them.
11.29: But Moses said unto him, Enviest thou for my sake? yea, would God that all the Lordes people were Prophets, and that the Lord would put his Spirit upon them.
11.30: And Moses returned into the host, he and the Elders of Israel.
11.31: Then there went foorth a wind from the Lord, and brought quailes from the Sea, and let them fall upon the camp, a dayes journey on this side, and a dayes journey on the other side, round about the host, and they were about two cubites above the earth.
11.32: Then the people arose, al that day, and all the night, and all the next day, and gathered the quailes: he that gathered the least, gathered ten Homers full, and they spred them abroad for their use round about the host.
11.33: While the flesh was yet between their teeth, before it was chewed, even the wrath of the Lord was kindled against the people, and the Lord smote the people with an exceeding great plague.
11.34: So the name of the place was called, Kibroth-hattaauah: for there they buried the people that fell a lusting.
11.35: From Kibroth-hattaauah ye people took their journey to Hazeroth, and abode at Hazeroth.

12.1: Afterward Miriam and Aaron spake against Moses, because of the woman of Ethiopia whom hee had maried (for hee had married a woman of Ethiopia)
12.2: And they said, What? hath the Lord spoken but onely by Moses? hath he not spoken also by us? and the Lord heard this.
12.3: (But Moses was a verie meek man, above all the men that were upon the earth)
12.4: And by and by the Lord sayd unto Moses, and unto Aaron, and unto Miriam, come out yee three unto the Tabernacle of the Congregation: and they three came forth.
12.5: Then the Lord came down in the pillar of the cloud, and stood in the door of the Tabernacle, and called Aaron and Miriam, and they both came forth.
12.6: And hee said, Hear now my wordes, If there be a Prophet of the Lord among you, I will be knowen to him by a vision, and will speak unto him by dream.
12.7: My servant Moses is not so, who is faithful in all mine house.
12.8: Unto him will I speak mouth to mouth, and by vision, and not in dark wordes, but hee shall see the similitude of the Lord. Wherefore then were ye not afraid to speak against my servant, even against Moses?
12.9: Thus the Lord was very angrie with them, and departed.
12.10: Also the cloud departed from the Tabernacle: and behold, Miriam was leprous like snow: and Aaron looked upon Miriam, and behold, she was leprous.
12.11: Then Aaron said unto Moses, Alas, my Lord, I beseech thee, lay not the sinne upon us, which we have foolishly committed and wherein we have sinned.
12.12: Let her not, I pray thee, be as one dead, of whom the flesh is half consumed, when he cometh out of his mothers womb.
12.13: Then Moses cryed unto the Lord, saying, O God, I beseech thee, heal her now.
12.14: And the Lord said unto Moses, If her father had spit in her face, should she not have been ashamed seven dayes? let her be shut out of the host seven dayes, and after she shall bee received.
12.15: So Miriam was shut out of the host seven dayes, and the people remooued not, till Miriam was brought in again.

13.1: Then afterward the people remooued from Hazeroth, and pitched in the wilderness of Paran.
13.2: And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
13.3: Send thou men out to search the land of Canaan which I give unto the children of Israel: of every tribe of their fathers shall ye send a man, such as are all rulers among them.
13.4: Then Moses sent them out of the wilderness of Paran at the commandement of the Lord: all those men were heades of the children of Israel.
13.5: Also their names are these: of the tribe of Reuben, Shammua the sonne of Zaccur:
13.6: Of the tribe of Simeon, Shaphat the sonne of Hori:
13.7: Of the tribe of Judah, Caleb the sonne of Jephunneh:
13.8: Of the tribe of Issachar, Igal the sonne of Joseph:
13.9: Of the tribe of Ephraim, Oshea the son of Nun:
13.10: Of the tribe of Beniamin, Palti the sonne of Raphu:
13.11: Of the tribe of Zebulun, Gaddiel the son of Sodi:
13.12: Of the tribe of Joseph, to wit, of the tribe of Manasseh, Gaddi the sonne of Susi:
13.13: Of the tribe of Dan, Ammiel the sonne of Gemalli:
13.14: Of the tribe of Asher, Sethur the sonne of Michael:
13.15: Of the tribe of Naphtali, Nahbi the sonne of Vophsi:
13.16: Of the tribe of Gad, Geuel the sonne of Machi.
13.17: These are the names of the men, which Moses sent to spie out the land: and Moses called ye name of Oshea the sonne of Nun, Jehoshua.
13.18: So Moses sent them to spie out the land of Canaan, and said unto them, Go up this way toward the South, and go up into the moutaines,
13.19: And consider the land what it is, and the people that dwel therein, whether they be strong or weak, either few or many,
13.20: Also what the land is that they dwell in, whether it be good or bad: and what cities they be, that they dwell in, whether they dwell in tents, or in walled townes:
13.21: And what the land is: whether it be fat or lean, whether there be trees therein, or not. And be of good courage, and bring of the fruit of the land (for then was the time of the first ripe grapes)
13.22: So they went up, and searched out the land, from the wilderness of Zin unto Rehob, to go to Hamath,
13.23: And they ascended toward the South, and came unto Hebron, where were Ahiman, Sheshai and Talmai, the sonnes of Anak. And Hebron was built seven yeere before Zoan in Egypt.
13.24: Then they came to the river of Eshcol, and cut down thence a branch with one cluster of grapes, and they bare it upon a bar between two, and brought of the pomegranates and of the figges.
13.25: That place was called the river Eshcol, because of the cluster of grapes, which the children of Israel cut down thence.
13.26: Then after fourtie dayes, they turned again from searching of the land.
13.27: And they went and came to Moses and to Aaron and unto al the Congregation of the children of Israel, in the wilderness of Paran, to Kadesh, and brought to the, and to all the Congregation tydings, and shewed them the fruit of the land.
13.28: And they told him, and said, We came unto the land whither thou hast sent us, and surely it floweth with milk and honie: and here is of the fruit of it.
13.29: Nevertheless the people be strong that dwell in the land, and the cities are walled and exceeding great: and moreover, we saw the sonnes of Anak there.
13.30: The Amalekites dwell in the South countrey, and the Hittites, and the Jebusites, and the Amorites dwell in the mountaines, and the Canaanites dwell by the sea, and by the coast of Iorden.
13.31: Then Caleb stilled the people before Moses, and said, Let us go up at once, and possess it: for vndoubtedly we shall overcome it.
13.32: But the men, that went up with him, said, we be not able to goe up against the people: for they are stronger then we.
13.33: So they brought up an evil report of the land which they had searched for the children of Israel, saying, The land which we have gone through to search it out, is a land that eateth up the inhabitants thereof: for all the people that we saw in it, are men of great stature.
13.34: For there we saw gyants, the sonnes of Anak, which come of the gyants, so that we seemed in our sight like grashoppers: and so wee were in their sight.

14.1: Then all ye Congregation lifted up their voice, and cryed: and the people wept that night,
14.2: And all the children of Israel murmured against Moses and Aaron: and the whole assemblie said unto them, Would God we had died in the land of Egypt, or in this wilderness: would God we were dead.
14.3: Wherefore now hath the Lord brought us into this land to fall upon the sword? our wives, and our children shall be a pray: were it not better for us to return into Egypt?
14.4: And they said one to another, Let us make a Captain and return into Egypt.
14.5: Then Moses and Aaron fell on their faces before all the assemblie of the Congregation of the children of Israel.
14.6: And Joshua the sonne of Nun, and Caleb the sonne of Jephunneh two of them that searched the land, rent their clothes,
14.7: And spake unto all the assemblie of the childre of Israel, saying, The land which we walked through to search it, is a very good land.
14.8: If the Lord love us, he will bring us into this land, and give it us, which is a land that floweth with milk and honie.
14.9: But rebel not ye against the Lord, neither fear ye the people of the land: for they are but bread for us: their shield is departed from the, and the Lord is with us, fear them not.
14.10: And all the multitude said, Stone them with stones: but the glory of the Lord appeared in the Tabernacle of the Congregation, before all the children of Israel.
14.11: And the Lord said unto Moses, How long will this people provoke me, and how long will it be, yer they beleeue me, for al the signes which I have shewed among them?
14.12: I will smite them with the pestilence and destroy them, and will make thee a greater nation and mightier then they.
14.13: But Moses said unto the Lord, When the Egyptians shall hear it, (for thou broughtest this people by thy power from among them)
14.14: Then they shall say to the inhabitants of this land, (for they have heard that thou, Lord, art among this people, and that thou, Lord, art seen face to face, and that thy cloud standeth over them, and that thou goest before them by day time in a pillar of a cloud, and in a pillar of fire by night)
14.15: That thou wilt kill this people as one man: so the heathen which have heard the fame of thee, shall thus say,
14.16: Because the Lord was not able to bring this people into the land, which he sware unto them, therefore hath he slain them in the wilderness.
14.17: And now, I beseech thee, let the power of my Lord be great, according as thou hast spoken, saying,
14.18: The Lord is slow to anger, and of great mercie, and forgiving iniquitie, and sinne, but not making the wicked innocent, and visiting the wickednes of the fathers upon the children, in the third and fourth generation:
14.19: Be merciful, I beseech thee, unto the iniquitie of this people, according to thy great mercie, and as thou hast forgiven this people from Egypt, even until now.
14.20: And the Lord said, I have forgiven it, according to thy request.
14.21: Notwithstanding, as I live, all the earth shall be filled with the glory of the Lord.
14.22: For all those men which have seen my glory, and my miracles which I did in Egypt, and in the wildernes, and have tempted me this ten times, and have not obeyed my voyce,
14.23: Certainely they shall not see the land, whereof I sware unto their fathers: neither shall any that provoke me, see it.
14.24: But my servant Caleb, because he had another spirit, and hath followed me stil, even him will I bring into the land, whither he went, and his seed shall inherit it.
14.25: Now the Amalekites and the Canaanites remain in the valley: wherefore turn back to morowe, and get you into the wilderness, by the way of the red Sea.
14.26: After, the Lord spake unto Moses and to Aaron, saying,
14.27: How long shall I suffer this wicked multitude to murmur against me? I have heard the murmurings of the children of Israel, which they murmur against me.
14.28: Tell them, As I live (saith the Lord) I wil surely do unto you, even as ye have spoken in mine eares.
14.29: Your carkeises shall fall in this wildernes, and all you that were counted through all your nombers, from twentie yeere old and above, which have murmured against me,
14.30: Ye shall not doubtles come into the land, for the which I lifted up mine hand, to make you dwell therein, save Caleb the sonne of Jephunneh, and Joshua the sonne of Nun.
14.31: But your children, (which ye said should be a pray) them will I bring in, and they shall know the land which ye have refused:
14.32: But even your carkeises shall fall in this wildernes,
14.33: And your children shall wander in the wilderness, fourtie yeeres, and shall bear your whoredomes, until your carkeises be wasted in the wilderness.
14.34: After the number of the dayes, in the which ye searched out the land, even fourtie dayes, every day for a yeere, shall ye bear your iniquity, for fourtie yeeres, and ye shall feel my breach of promise.
14.35: I the Lord have said, Certainely I will doe so to all this wicked company, that are gathered together against me: for in this wilderness they shall be consumed, and there they shall die.
14.36: And the men which Moses had sent to search the land (which, when they came again, made all the people to murmur against him, and brought up a slander upon the land)
14.37: Even those men that did bring up that vile slander upon the land, shall die by a plague before the Lord.
14.38: But Joshua the sonne of Nun, and Caleb the sonne of Jephunneh, of those men that went to search the land, shall live.
14.39: Then Moses told these sayings unto all the children of Israel, and the people sorowed greatly.
14.40: And they rose up earely in the morning, and gate them up into the toppe of the mountain, saying, Loe, we be readie, to goe up to the place which the Lord hath promised: for wee have sinned.
14.41: But Moses said, Wherefore transgress yee thus the commandement of the Lord? it will not so come well to pass.
14.42: Goe not up (for the Lord is not among you) lest ye be overthrow before your enemies.
14.43: For the Amalekites and the Canaanites are there before you, and ye shall fall by the sword: for in as much as ye are turned away from the Lord, the Lord also will not be with you.
14.44: Yet they presumed obstinately to goe up to the top of the mountain: but the Ark of the covenant of the Lord, and Moses departed not out of the camp.
14.45: Then the Amalekites and the Canaanites, which dwelt in that mountain, came down and smote them, and consumed them unto Hormah.

15.1: And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
15.2: Speak unto the children of Israel, and say unto them, Whe ye be come into the land of your habitations, which I give unto you,
15.3: And will make an offring by fire unto the Lord, a burnt offring or a sacrifice to fulfil a vow, or a free offring, or in your feastes, to make a sweet sauour unto the Lord of the heard, or of the flock.
15.4: Then let him that offreth his offring unto the Lord, bring a meat offring of a tenth deal of fine flowre, mingled with the fourth part of an Hin of oyle.
15.5: Also thou shalt prepare ye fourth part of an Hin of wine to be powred on a lamb, appointed for the burnt offring or any offring.
15.6: And for a ram, thou shalt for a meat offring, prepare two tenth deales of fine flour, mingled with the third part of an Hin of oyle.
15.7: And for a drink-offering, thou shalt offer the third part of an Hin of wine, for a sweet sauour unto the Lord.
15.8: And when thou preparest a bullock for a burnt offring, or for a sacrifice to fulfil a vow or a peace offring to the Lord,
15.9: Then let him offer with ye bullock a meat offring of three tenth deales of fine flour, mingled with half an Hin of oyle.
15.10: And thou shalt bring for a drink offring half an Hin of wine, for an offring made by fire of a sweet sauour unto the Lord.
15.11: Thus shall it be done for a bullock, or for a ram, or for a lamb, or for a kid.
15.12: According to the nomber that yee prepare to offer, so shall yee doe to every one according to their nomber.
15.13: All that are borne of the countrey, shall do these things thus, to offer an offring made by fire of sweet sauour unto the Lord.
15.14: And if a stranger soiourne with you, or whosoever bee among you in your generations, and will make an offring by fire of a sweet sauour unto the Lord, as ye do, so hee shall doe.
15.15: One ordinance shalbe both for you of the Congregation, and also for the stranger that dwelleth with you, even an ordinance for ever in your generations: as you are, so shall the stranger bee before the Lord.
15.16: One Law and one maner shall serve both for you and for the stranger that soiourneth with you.
15.17: And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
15.18: Speak unto the children of Israel, and say unto them, When ye be come into the land, to the which I bring you,
15.19: And when ye shall eat of the bread of the land, ye shall offer an heave offring unto ye Lord.
15.20: Ye shall offer up a cake of the first of your dowe for an heave offring: as the heave offring of the barn, so ye shall lift it up.
15.21: Of the first of your dowe ye shall give unto the Lord an heave offring in your generations.
15.22: And if ye have erred, and not observed all these commandements, which the Lord hath spoken unto Moses,
15.23: Even all that the Lord hath commanded you by the hand of Moses, from the first day that the Lord commanded Moses, and hence forward among your generations:
15.24: And if so be that ought be committed ignorantly of the Congregation, then all ye Congregatio shall give a bullock for a burnt offring, for a sweet sauour unto the Lord, with the meat offring and drink offring thereto, according to the maner, and an hee goat for a sinne offring.
