15.25: And the Priest shall make an atonement for al the Congregation of the children of Israel, and it shalbe forgiven them: for it is ignorance: and they shall bring their offring for an offring made by fire unto the Lord, and their sinne offering before the Lord for their ignorance.
15.26: Then it shalbe forgiven all the Congregation of the children of Israel, and the stranger that dwelleth among them: for all the people were in ignorance.
15.27: But if any one person sinne through ignorance, then he shall bring a she goat of a yeere old for a sinne offring.
15.28: And the Priest shall make an atonement for the ignorant person, when hee sinneth by ignorance before the Lord, to make reconciliation for him: and it shalbe forgiven him.
15.29: He that is borne among the children of Israel, and the stranger that dwelleth among them, shall have both one law, who so doth sinne by ignorance.
15.30: But the person that doeth ought presumptuously, whether he be borne in the land, or a stranger, the same blasphemeth the Lord: therefore that person shalbe cut off from among his people,
15.31: Because he hath despised the word of the Lord, and hath broken his commandement: that person shalbe utterly cut off: his iniquitie shalbe upon him.
15.32: And while the children of Israel were in the wilderness, they found a man that gathered stickes upon the Sabbath day.
15.33: And they that found him gathering sticks, brought him unto Moses and to Aaron, and unto all the Congregation,
15.34: And they put him ward: for it was not declared what should be done unto him.
15.35: Then the Lord said unto Moses, This man shall dye the death: and let al the multitude stone him with stones without the host.
15.36: And all the Congregation brought him without the host, and stoned him with stones, and he died, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
15.37: And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
15.38: Speak unto the children of Israel, and bid them that they make them fringes upon the borders of their garments throughout their generations, and put upon the fringes of the borders a ryband of blew silk.
15.39: And ye shall have the fringes, that when ye look upon them, ye may remember all the commandemets of the Lord, and do them: and that ye seek not after your own heart, nor after your own eyes, after the which ye go a whoring;
15.40: That yee may remember and doe all my commandements, and bee holy unto your God.
15.41: I am the Lord your God, which brought you out of the land of Egypt, to bee your God: I am the Lord your God.

16.1: Now Korah the sonne of Izhar, the sonne of Kohath, the sonne of Levi went apart with Dathan, and Abiram the sonnes of Eliab, and On the sonne of Peleth, the sonnes of Reuben:
16.2: And they rose up against Moses, with certain of the children of Israel, two hundreth and fiftie captaines of the assemblie, famous in the Congregation, and men of renoume,
16.3: Who gathered themselves together against Moses, and against Aaron, and sayde unto them, Ye take too much upon you, seeing all the Congregation is holie, every one of them, and the Lord is among them: wherfore then lift ye your selves above the Congregation of the Lord?
16.4: But when Moses heard it, hee fell upon his face,
16.5: And spake to Korah and unto all his companie, saying, To morow the Lord will shew who is his, and who is holy, and who ought to approche neere unto him: and whom he hath chosen, hee will cause to come neere to him.
16.6: This doe therefore, Take you censers, both Korah, and all his companie,
16.7: And put fire therein, and put incense in the before the Lord to morowe: and the man whom the Lord doeth chuse, the same shalbe holie: ye take too much upon you, ye sonnes of Levi.
16.8: Again Moses said unto Korah, Hear, I pray you, ye sonnes of Levi.
16.9: Seemeth it a small thing unto you that the God of Israel hath separated you from the multitude of Israel, to take you neere to himself, to doe the service of the Tabernacle of the Lord, and to stand before the Congregation and to minister unto them?
16.10: He hath also taken thee to him, and all thy brethren the sonnes of Levi with thee, and seek ye the office of the Priest also?
16.11: For which cause, thou, and all thy companie are gathered together against the Lord: and what is Aaron, that ye murmur against him?
16.12: And Moses sent to call Dathan, and Abiram the sonnes of Eliab: who answered, We will not come up.
16.13: Is it a small thing that thou hast brought us out of a land that floweth with milk and honie, to kill us in the wilderness, except thou make thy self lord and ruler over us also?
16.14: Also thou hast not brought us unto a land that floweth with milk and honie, neither given us inheritance of fieldes and vineyardes: wilt thou put out the eyes of these men? we will not come up.
16.15: Then Moses waxed verie angry, and said unto the Lord, Look not unto their offring: I have not taken so much as an ass from them, neither have I hurt any of them.
16.16: And Moses said unto Korah, Bee thou and al thy companie before the Lord: both thou, they, and Aaron to morowe:
16.17: And take every man his censor, and put incense in them, and bring ye every man his censor before the Lord, two hundreth and fiftie censors: thou also and Aaron, every one his censor.
16.18: So they took every man his censor, and put fire in them, and laid incense thereon, and stood in the door of the Tabernacle of the Congregation with Moses and Aaron.
16.19: And Korah gathered all the multitude against them unto the door of the Tabernacle of the Congregation: then the glorie of the Lord appeared unto all the Congregation.
16.20: And the Lord spake unto Moses and to Aaron, saying,
16.21: Separate your selves from among this Cogregation, that I may consume them at once.
16.22: And they fell upon their faces and said, O God the God of the spirits, of all flesh, hath not one man onely sinned, and wilt thou bee wroth with all the Congregation?
16.23: And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
16.24: Speak unto the Congregation and say, Get you away from about the Tabernacle of Korah, Dathan and Abiram.
16.25: Then Moses rose up, and went unto Dathan and Abiram, and the Elders of Israel followed him.
16.26: And he spake unto the Congregation, saying, Depart, I pray you, from the tentes of these wicked men, and touch nothing of theirs, lest ye perish in all their sinnes.
16.27: So they gate them away from the Tabernacle of Korah, Dathan and Abiram on euerie side: and Dathan, and Abiram came out and stood in the door of their tentes with their wives, and their sonnes, and their little children.
16.28: And Moses said, Hereby yee shall know that the Lord hath sent me to do all these works: for I have not done them of mine own mind.
16.29: If these men die the common death of all men, or if they be visited after the visitation of all men, the Lord hath not sent me.
16.30: But if the Lord make a new thing, and the earth open her mouth, and swallow them up with all that they have, and they goe down quick into ye pit, then ye shall understand that these men have provoked the Lord.
16.31: And assoone as he had made an end of speaking all these wordes, even the ground clave asunder that was under them,
16.32: And the earth opened her mouth, and swallowed them up, with their families, and all the men that were with Korah, and all their goods.
16.33: So they and all that they had, went down alive into the pit, and the earth covered them: so they perished from among the Congregation.
16.34: And all Israel that were about them, fled at the crie of them: for they said, Let us flee, least the earth swalow us up.
16.35: But there came out a fire from the Lord, and consumed the two hundreth and fiftie men that offred the incense.
16.36: And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
16.37: Speak unto Eleazar, the sonne of Aaron the Priest, that he take up the censers out of the burning, and scatter the fire beyond the altar: for they are halowed,
16.38: The censers, I say, of these sinners, that destroyed themselves: and let them make of them broad plates for a covering of the Altar: for they offered them before the Lord, therefore they shalbe holy, and they shall be a sign unto the children of Israel.
16.39: Then Eleazar the Priest took the brasen censers, which they, that were burnt, had offred, and made broad plates of them for a covering of the Altar.
16.40: It is a remembrance unto the children of Israel, that no stranger which is not of the seed of Aaron, come neere to offer incense before the Lord, that he be not like Korah and his company, as the Lord said to him by the hand of Moses.
16.41: But on the morowe all the multitude of the children of Israel murmured against Moses and against Aaron, saying, Ye have killed the people of the Lord.
16.42: And when the Congregation was gathered against Moses and against Aaron, then they turned their faces toward the Tabernacle of the Congregation: and behold, the cloud covered it, and the glory of the Lord appeared.
16.43: Then Moses and Aaron were come before the Tabernacle of the Congregation.
16.44: And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
16.45: Get you up from among this Congregation: for I wil consume them quickly: then they fell upon their faces.
16.46: And Moses said unto Aaron, Take the censer and put fire therein of the Altar, and put therein incense, and goe quickly unto the Congregation, and make an atonement for them: for there is wrath gone out from the Lord: the plague is begunne.
16.47: Then Aaron took as Moses commanded him, and ranne into the middes of the Congregation, and behold, the plague was begun among the people, and hee put in incense, and made an atonement for the people.
16.48: And when hee stood between the dead, and them that were alive, the plague was stayed.
16.49: So they died of this plague fourtene thousand and seven hundreth, beside them that dyed in the conspiracie of Korah.
16.50: And Aaron went again unto Moses before the door of the Tabernacle of the Congregation, and the plague was stayed.

17.1: And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
17.2: Speak unto the children of Israel, and take of every one of them a rod, after the house of their fathers, of all their princes according to the familie of their fathers, even twelve rods: and thou shalt write every mans name upon his rod.
17.3: And write Aarons name upon the rod of Levi: for every rod shalbe for the head of the house of their fathers.
17.4: And thou shalt put them in the Tabernacle of the Congregation, before the Ark of the Testimonie, where I wil declare my self to you.
17.5: And the mans rod, whom I chuse, shall blossom: and I will make cease from mee the grudgings of the children of Israel, which grudge against you.
17.6: Then Moses spake unto the children of Israel, and al their princes gave him a rod, one rod for every Prince, according to the houses of their fathers, even twelve rods, and the rod of Aaron was among their roddes.
17.7: And Moses layde the rods before the Lord in the Tabernacle of the Testimonie.
17.8: And when Moses on the morow went into the Tabernacle of the Testimonie, behold, the rod of Aaron for the house of Levi was budded, and brought forth buddes, and brought forth blossoms, and bare ripe almondes.
17.9: Then Moses brought out all the rods from before the Lord unto all the children of Israel: and they looked upon them, and took every man his rod.
17.10: After, the Lord said unto Moses, Bring Aarons rod again before the Testimonie to bee kept for a token to the rebellious children, and thou shalt cause their murmurings to cease from me, that they dye not.
17.11: So Moses did as the Lord had commanded him: so did he.
17.12: And the children of Israel spake unto Moses, saying, Behold, we are dead, we perish, we are all lost:
17.13: Whosoever cometh neere, or approcheth to the Tabernacle of the Lord, shall dye: shall we be consumed and dye?

18.1: And the Lord sayd unto Aaron, Thou, and thy sonnes and thy fathers house with thee, shall bear the iniquitie of the Sanctuarie: both thou and thy sonnes with thee shall bear the iniquitie of your Priestes office.
18.2: And bring also with thee thy brethren of the tribe of Levi of ye familie of thy father, which shalbe ioyned with thee, and minister unto thee: but thou, and thy sonnes with thee shall minister before the Tabernacle of the Testimonie:
18.3: And they shall keep thy charge, even the charge of all the Tabernacle: but they shall not come neere the instruments of the Sanctuary, nor to the altar, lest they die, both they and you:
18.4: And they shalbe ioyned with thee, and keep the charge of the Tabernacle of the Congregation for all the service of the Tabernacle: and no stranger shall come neere unto you:
18.5: Therefore shall ye keep the charge of the Sanctuarie, and the charge of the altar: so there shall fall no more wrath upon the children of Israel.
18.6: For lo, I have taken your brethren the Levites from among the children of Israel, which as a gift of yours, are given unto the Lord, to do the service of the Tabernacle of the Congregation.
18.7: But thou, and thy sonnes with thee shall keep your Priestes office for all things of the altar, and within the vail: therefore shall ye serve: for I have made your Priestes office an office of service: therefore the stranger that cometh neere, shalbe slayne.
18.8: Again the Lord spake unto Aaron, Behold, I have given thee the keeping of mine offrings, of all the hallowed things of the children of Israel: unto thee I have given them for the anoyntings sake, and to thy sonnes, for a perpetual ordinance.
18.9: This shalbe thine of the most holy things, reserved from the fire: all their offering of all their meat offring, and of all their sinne offring, and of all their trespass offring, which they bring unto me, that shalbe most holy unto thee, and to thy sonnes.
18.10: In the most holy place shalt thou eat it: every male shall eat of it: it is holy unto thee.
18.11: This also shalbe thine: the heave offering of their gift, with all the shake offerings of the children of Israel: I have given them unto thee and to thy sonnes and to thy daughters with thee, to be a duetie for ever al the clean in thine house shall eat of it.
18.12: All the fat of the oyle, and all the fat of the wine, and of the wheat, which they shall offer unto the Lord for their first fruites, I have given them unto thee.
18.13: And the first ripe of al that is in their land, which they shall bring unto Lord, shalbe thine: all the clean in thine house shall eat of it.
18.14: Every thing separate from the common use in Israel, shalbe thine.
18.15: All that first openeth the matrice of any flesh, which they shall offer unto the Lord, of man or beast, shalbe thine: but the first borne of man shalt thou redeem, and the first borne of the vncleane beast shalt thou redeem.
18.16: And those that are to bee redeemed, shalt thou redeem from the age of a moneth, according to thy estimation, for the money of five shekels, after the shekel of the Sanctuarie, which is twentie gerahs.
18.17: But the first borne of a kow, or the first borne of a sheep, or the first borne of a goat shalt thou not redeem: for they are holy: thou shalt sprinkle their blood at the altar, and thou shalt burn their fat: it is a sacrifice made by fire for a sweet sauour unto the Lord.
18.18: And the flesh of them shalbe thine, as the shake breast, and as the right shoulder shalbe thine.
18.19: All the heave offrings of the holy things which the children of Israel shall offer unto the Lord, have I given thee, and thy sonnes, and thy daughters with thee, to be a duetie for ever: it is a perpetual covenant of salt before the Lord, to thee, and to thy seed with thee.
18.20: And the Lord sayde unto Aaron, Thou shalt have none inheritance in their land, neyther shalt thou have any part among them: I am thy part and thine inheritance among the children of Israel.
18.21: For behold, I have given the children of Levi all the tenth in Israel for an inheritance, for their service which they serve in the Tabernacle of the Congregation.
18.22: Neyther shall the children of Israel any more come neere the Tabernacle of the Congregation, lest they susteine sinne, and die.
18.23: But the Levites shall do the service in the Tabernacle of the Congregation, and they shall bear their sinne: it is a law for ever in your generations, that among the children of Israel they possess none inheritance.
18.24: For the tythes of the children of Israel, which they shall offer as an offring unto the Lord, I have given the Levites for an inheritance: therfore I have said unto them, Among the children of Israel ye shall possess none inheritance.
18.25: And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
18.26: Speak also unto the Levites and say unto them, When ye shall take of the children of Israel the tithes, which I have given you of them for your inheritance, then shall ye take an heave offring of that same for the Lord, even the tenth part of the tithe.
18.27: And your heave offering shalbe reckened unto you, as the corn of the barn, or as the abundance of the wine press.
18.28: So ye shall also offer an heave offring unto the Lord of all your tithes, which ye shall receive of the children of Israel, and ye shall give thereof the Lords heave offring to Aaron the Priest.
18.29: Ye shall offer of all your gifts al the Lords heave offrings: of all the fat of the same shall ye offer the holy things thereof.
18.30: Therefore thou shalt say unto them, When ye have offred the fat thereof, then it shalbe couted unto the Levites, as the encrease of the corn floor, or as the encrease of the wine press.
18.31: And ye shall eat it in al places, ye, and your housholdes: for it is your wages for your service in the Tabernacle of the Congregation.
18.32: And ye shall bear no sinne by the reason of it, when ye have offred the fatte of it: neither shall ye pollute the holy things of the children of Israel, lest ye die.

19.1: And the Lord spake to Moses, and to Aaron, saying,
19.2: This is the ordinance of the law, which the Lord hath commanded, saying, Speak unto the children of Israel that they bring thee a red kow without blemish, wherein is no spot, upon the which never came yoke.
19.3: And ye shall give her unto Eleazar ye Priest, that hee may bring her without the host, and cause her to be slain before his face.
19.4: Then shall Eleazar the Priest take of her blood with his finger, and sprinkle it before the Tabernacle of the Congregation seven times,
19.5: And cause the kow to be burnt in his sight: with her skinne, and her flesh, and her blood, and her doung shall he burn her.
19.6: Then shall the Priest take cedar wood, and hyssop and skarlet lace, and cast them in the mids of the fire where the kow burneth.
19.7: Then shall the Priest wash his clothes, and he shall wash his flesh in water, and then come into the host, and the Priest shalbe vncleane unto the even.
19.8: Also he that burneth her, shall wash his clothes in water, and wash his flesh in water, and be vncleane until even.
19.9: And a man, that is clean, shall take up the ashes of the kow, and put them without the host in a clean place: and it shalbe kept for the Congregation of the children of Israel for a sprinkling water: it is a sinne offring.
19.10: Therefore he that gathereth the ashes of the kow, shall wash his clothes, and remain vncleane until even: and it shalbe unto the children of Israel, and unto the stranger that dwelleth among them, a statute for ever.
19.11: Hee that toucheth the dead body of any man, shalbe vncleane even seven dayes.
19.12: Hee shall purifie himself therewith the third day, and the seventh day he shall be clean: but if he purifie not himself the third day, then the seventh day he shall not be clean.
19.13: Whosoever toucheth ye corps of any man that is dead, and purgeth not himself, defileth the Tabernacle of the Lord, and that person shall be cut off from Israel, because the sprinkling water was not sprinkled upon him: he shall be vncleane, and his vncleannesse shall remain still upon him.
19.14: This is the law, Whe a man dieth in a tent, all that come into the tent, and all that is in the tent, shalbe vncleane seven dayes,
19.15: And all the vessels that bee open, which have no covering fastened upon them, shall be vncleane.
19.16: Also whosoever toucheth one that is slain with a sword in the field, or a dead person, or a bone of a dead man, or a grave, shall be vncleane seven dayes.
19.17: Therfore for an vncleane person they shall take of the burnt ashes of the sinne offring, and pure water shalbe put thereto in a vessel.
19.18: And a clean person shall take hyssop and dip it in the water, and sprinkle it upon the tent, and upon all the vessels, and on the persons that were therein, and upon him that touched ye bone, or the slayne, or the dead, or the grave.
19.19: And the clean person shall sprinkle upon the vncleane the third day, and the seventh day, and hee shall purifie him self the seventh day, and wash his clothes, and wash himself in water, and shalbe clean at even.
19.20: But the man that is vncleane and purifieth not himself, that person shalbe cut off from among the Congregation, because hee hath defiled the Sanctuarie of the Lord: and the sprinkling water hath not been sprinkled upon him: therefore shall he be vncleane.
19.21: And it shalbe a perpetual law unto them, that he that sprinkleth the sprinkling water, shall wash his clothes: also hee that toucheth the sprinkling water, shalbe vncleane until even.
19.22: And whatsoever the vncleane person toucheth, shall be vncleane: and the person that toucheth him, shalbe vncleane until the even.

20.1: Then the children of Israel came with ye whole Congregation to the desert of Zin in the first moneth, and the people abode at Cadesh: where Miriam died, and was buried there.
20.2: But there was no water for the Congregation, and they assembled them selves against Moses and against Aaron.
20.3: And the people chode with Moses, and spake, saying, Would God we had perished, when our brethren died before the Lord.
20.4: Why have ye thus brought the Congregation of the Lord unto his wilderness, that both we, and our cattell should die there?
20.5: Wherefore now have yee made us to come up from Egypt, to bring us into this miserable place, which is no place of seed, nor figges, nor vines, nor pomegranates? neither is there any water to drink.
20.6: Then Moses and Aaron went from the assemblie unto the door of the Tabernacle of the Congregation, and fell upon their faces: and the glory of the Lord appeared unto them.
20.7: And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
20.8: Take the rod, and gather thou and thy brother Aaron the Congregation together, and speak yee unto the rock before their eyes, and it shall give foorth his water, and thou shalt bring them water out of the rock: so thou shalt give the Congregation, and their beastes drink.
20.9: Then Moses took the rod from before the Lord, as he had commanded him.
20.10: And Moses and Aaron gathered the Congregation together before the rock, and Moses sayd unto them, Hear now, ye rebels: shall we bring you water out of this rock?
20.11: Then Moses lift up his hand, and with his rod he smote the rock twise, and the water came out aboundantly: so the Congregation, and their beastes drank.
20.12: Again the Lord spake unto Moses, and to Aaron, Because ye beleeued me not, to sanctifie mee in the presence of the children of Israel, therefore ye shall not bring this Congregation into the land which I have given them.
20.13: This is the water of Meribah, because the children of Israel strove with the Lord, and hee was sanctified in them.
20.14: Then Moses sent messengers from Kadesh unto the king of Edom, saying, Thus sayth thy brother Israel, Thou knowest all the travail that we have had,
20.15: How our fathers went down into Egypt, and we dwelt in Egypt a long time, where the Egyptians handled us evil and our fathers.
20.16: But when we cried unto the Lord, he heard our voyce, and sent an Angel, and hath brought us out of Egypt, and behold, wee are in the citie Kadesh, in thine utmost border.
20.17: I pray thee that we may pass through thy countrey: we will not goe through the fieldes nor the vineyardes, neither will we drink of the water of the welles: we will goe by the kings way, and neither turn unto the right hand nor to the left, until we be past thy borders.
20.18: And Edom answered him, Thou shalt not pass by mee, least I come out against thee with the sword.
20.19: Then the children of Israel said unto him, We will goe up by the hie way: and if I and my cattell drink of thy water, I will then pay for it: I will onely (without any harm) goe through on my feet.
20.20: Hee answered again, Thou shalt not goe through. The Edom came out against him with much people, and with a mightie power.
20.21: Thus Edom denyed to give Israel passage through his countrey: wherefore Israel turned away from him.
20.22: And when the children of Israel with al the Congregation departed from Kadesh, they came unto the mount Hor.
20.23: And the Lord spake unto Moses and to Aaron in the mount Hor neere the coast of the land of Edom, saying,
20.24: Aaron shall be gathered unto his people: for hee shall not enter into the land, which I have given unto the children of Israel, because ye disobeyed my commandement at the water of Meribah.
20.25: Take Aaron and Eleazar his sonne, and bring them up into the mount Hor,
20.26: And cause Aaron to put off his garmentes and put them upon Eleazar his sonne: for Aaron shall be gathered to his fathers, and shall die there.
20.27: And Moses did as the Lord had commanded: and they went up into the mount Hor, in the sight of all the Congregation.
20.28: And Moses put off Aarons clothes, and put them upon Eleazar his sonne: so Aaron dyed there in the top of the mount: and Moses and Eleazar came down from off the mount.
20.29: When al the Congregation saw that Aaron was dead, al the house of Israel wept for Aaron thirtie dayes.

21.1: When King Arad the Canaanite, which dwelt toward the South, heard tel that Israel came by the way of the spies, then fought hee against Israel, and took of them prysoners.
21.2: So Israel vowed a vow unto the Lord, and said, If thou wilt deliver and give this people into mine hand, then I wil utterly destroy their cities.
21.3: And the Lord heard the voyce of Israel, and delivered them the Canaanites: and they utterly destroied them and their cities, and called ye name of the place Hormah.
21.4: After, they departed from the mount Hor by the way of the red Sea, to compass the land of Edom: and the people were sore grieved because of the way.
21.5: And the people spake against God and against Moses, saying, Wherefore have ye brought us out of Egypt, to die in the wilderness? for here is neither bread nor water, and our soul lotheth this light bread.
21.6: Wherefore the Lord sent fierie serpents among ye people, which stung the people: so that many of the people of Israel died.
21.7: Therefore the people came to Moses and said, We have sinned: for wee have spoken against the Lord, and against thee: pray to the Lord, that he take away the serpents from us: and Moses prayed for the people.
21.8: And the Lord said unto Moses, Make thee a fiery serpent, and set it up for a sign, that as many as are bitten, may look upon it, and live.
21.9: So Moses made a serpent of brass, and set it up for a sign: and when a serpent had bitten a man, then he looked to the serpent of brass, and lived.
21.10: And ye children of Israel departed thence, and pitched in Oboth.
21.11: And they departed from Oboth, and pitched in lie-abarim, in the wilderness, which is before Moab on the Eastside.
21.12: They removed thence, and pitched upon the river of Zared.
21.13: Thence they departed, and pitched on the other side of Arnon, which is in the wilderness, and cometh out of the coasts of the Amorites: (for Arnon is the border of Moab, between the Moabites and the Amorites)
21.14: Wherefore it shall be spoken in the book of the battels of the Lord, what thing he did in the red sea, and in the rivers of Arnon,
21.15: And at the stream of the rivers that goeth down to the dwelling of Ar, and lieth upon the border of Moab.
21.16: And from thence they turned to Beer: the same is the well where the Lord said unto Moses, Assemble the people, and I wil give them water.
21.17: Then Israel sang this song, Rise up well, sing ye unto it.
21.18: The princes digged this well, the captaines of the people digged it, even the law giver, with their staves. And from the wilderness they came to Mattanah,
21.19: And from Mattanah to Nahaliel, and from Nahaliel to Bamoth,
21.20: And from Bamoth in the valley, that is in the plain of Moab, to the top of Pisgah that looketh toward Jeshimon.
21.21: Then Israel sent messengers unto Sihon, King of the Amorites, saying,
21.22: Let me goe through thy land: we wil not turn aside into the fieldes, nor into the vineyardes, neither drink of the waters of ye welles: we will goe by the kings way, until we be past thy countrey.
21.23: But Sihon gave Israel no licence to pass through his countrey, but Sihon assembled all his people, and went out against Israel into the wilderness: and he came to Iahoz, and fought against Israel.
21.24: But Israel smote him with the edge of the sword, and conquered his land, from Arnon unto Iabok, even unto ye children of Ammon: for the border of the children of Ammon was strong.
21.25: And Israel took al these cities, and dwelt in all the cities of the Amorites in Heshbon and in all the villages thereof.
21.26: For Heshbon was the citie of Sihon the king of the Amorites, which had fought beforetime against the king of the Moabites, and had taken al his land out of his hand, even unto Arnon.
21.27: Wherefore they that speak in prouerbes, say, Come to Heshbon, let the citie of Sihon bee built and repaired:
21.28: For a fire is gone out of Heshbon, and a flame from the citie of Sihon, and hath consumed Ar of the Moabites, and the lords of Bamoth in Arnon.
21.29: Wo be to thee, Moab: O people of Chemosh, thou art undone: he hath suffered his sonnes to be pursued, and his daughters to be in captiuitie to Sihon the king of the Amorites.
21.30: Their empire also is lost from Heshbon unto Dibon, and wee have destroyed them unto Nophah, which reacheth unto Medeba.
21.31: Thus Israel dwelt in the land of the Amorites.
21.32: And Moses sent to search out Jaazer, and they took the townes belonging thereto, and rooted out the Amorites that were there.
21.33: And they turned and went up toward Bashan: and Og the King of Bashan came out against them, hee, and all his people, to fight at Edrei.
21.34: Then the Lord said unto Moses, Fear him not: for I have delivered him into thine hand and all his people, and his land: and thou shalt do to him as thou diddest unto Sihon the king of the Amorites, which dwelt at Heshbon.
21.35: They smote him therefore, and his sonnes, and all his people, until there was none left him: so they conquered his land.

22.1: After, the children of Israel departed and pitched in the plain of Moab on the other side of Iorden from Jericho.
22.2: Now Balak the sonne of Zippor saw all that Israel had done to the Amorites.
22.3: And the Moabites were sore afraid of the people, because they were many, and Moab fretted against the children of Israel.
22.4: Therfore Moab said unto the Elders of Midian, Now shall this multitude lick up all that are round about us, as an oxe licketh up ye grass of the field: and Balak the sonne of Zippor was King of the Moabites at that time.
22.5: Hee sent messengers therefore unto Balaam the sonne of Beor to Pethor (which is by the river of the land of the children of his folk) to call him, saying, Behold, there is a people come out of Egypt, which cover the face of the earth, and lye over against me.
22.6: Come now therefore, I pray thee, and curse me this people (for they are stronger then I) so it may be that I shall be able to smite them, and to drive them out of the land: for I know that hee, whom thou blessest, is blessed, and he whom thou cursest, shall be cursed.
22.7: And the Elders of Moab, and the Elders of Midian departed, having the reward of the soothsaying in their hand, and they came unto Balaam, and told him the wordes of Balak.
22.8: Who answered them, Tary here this night, and I will give you an answer, as the Lord shall say unto mee. So the princes of Moab abode with Balaam.
22.9: Then God came unto Balaam, and sayde, What men are these with thee?
22.10: And Baalam said unto God, Balak ye sonne of Zippor, king of Moab hath set unto me, saying,
22.11: Behold, there is a people come out of Egypt and covereth the face of the earth: come now, curse them for my sake: so it may be that I shalbe able to overcome them in battell, and to drive them out.
22.12: And God said unto Balaam, Go not thou with them, neither curse the people, for they are blessed.
22.13: And Balaam rose up in the morning, and sayde unto ye princes of Balak, Return unto your land: for the Lord hath refused to give me leave to go with you.
22.14: So the princes of Moab rose up, and went unto Balak, and sayd, Balaam hath refused to come with us.
22.15: Balak yet sent again moe princes, and more honourable then they.
22.16: Who came to Balaam, and sayde to him, Thus saith Balak the sonne of Zippor, Bee not thou staied, I pray thee, from coming unto me.
22.17: For I wil promote thee unto great honour, and wil do whatsoever thou sayest unto me: come therefore, I pray thee, curse me this people.
22.18: And Balaam answered, and sayde unto the servants of Balak, If Balak would give me his house full of silver and gold, I can not goe beyond the word of the Lord my God, to doe less or more.
22.19: But now, I pray you, tary here this night, that I may wit, what the Lord will say unto mee more.
22.20: And God came unto Balaam by night, and sayd unto him, If the men come to call thee, rise up, and goe with them: but onely what thing I say unto thee, that shalt thou doe.
22.21: So Balaam rose up early, and sadled his ass, and went with the princes of Moab.
22.22: And ye wrath of God was kindled, because he went: and the Angel of the Lord stood in the way to be against him, as he rode upon his ass, and his two servants were with him.
22.23: And when the ass saw the Angel of the Lord stand in the way, and his sword drawen in his hand, the ass turned out of the way and went into the field, but Balaam smote the ass, to turn her into the way.
22.24: Again the Angel of the Lord stood in a path of the vineyardes, having a wall on the one side, and a wall on the other.
22.25: And when the ass saw the Angel of the Lord, she thrust her self unto the wall, and dasht Balaams foot against the wall: wherefore hee smote her again.
22.26: Then the Angel of the Lord went further, and stood in a narowe place, where was no way to turn, either to the right hand, or to the left.
22.27: And when the ass saw the Angel of the Lord, she lay down under Balaam: therefore Balaam was very wroth, and smote the ass with a staff.
22.28: Then the Lord opened the mouth of the ass, and she said unto Balaam, What have I done unto thee, that thou hast smitten me now three times?
22.29: And Balaam said unto the ass, Because thou hast mocked me: I would there were a sword in mine hand, for now would I kill thee.
22.30: And the ass said unto Balaam, Am not I thine ass, which thou hast ridden upon since thy first time unto this day? have I used at any time to doe thus unto thee? Who said, Nay.
22.31: And the Lord opened the eyes of Balaam, and he saw the Angel of the Lord standing in the way with his sword drawen in his hand: then he bowed him self, and fell flat on his face.
22.32: And the Angel of the Lord said unto him, Wherefore hast thou now smitten thine ass three times? behold, I came out to withstand thee, because thy way is not straight before me.
22.33: But the ass saw me, and turned from me now three times: for els, if she had not turned from me, surely I had even now slain thee, and saved her alive.
22.34: Then Balaam said unto the Angel of the Lord, I have sinned: for I wist not that thou stoodest in the way against me: now therefore if it displease thee, I will turn home again.
22.35: But the Angel said unto Balaam, Go with the men: but what I say unto thee, that shalt thou speak. So Balaam went with ye princes of Balak.
22.36: And when Balak heard that Balaam came, he went out to meet him unto a citie of Moab, which is in the border of Arnon, even in the utmost coast.
22.37: Then Balak said unto Balaam, Did I not send for thee to call thee? Wherefore camest thou not unto me? am I not able in deed to promote thee unto honour?
22.38: And Balaam made answer unto Balak, Lo, I am come unto thee, and can I now say any thing at all? the word that God putteth in my mouth, that shall I speak.
22.39: So Balaam went with Balak, and they came unto the citie of Huzoth.
22.40: Then Balak offred bullockes, and sheep, and sent thereof to Balaam, and to the princes that were with him.
22.41: And on the morowe Balak took Balaam, and brought him up into the hie places of Baal, that thence hee might see the utmost part of the people.

23.1: And Balaam sayd unto Balak, Build me here seven altars, and prepare me here seven bullockes, and seven rammes.
23.2: And Balak did as Balaam sayd, and Balak and Balaam offred on every altar a bullock and a ramme.
23.3: Then Balaam sayde unto Balak, Stand by the burnt offring, and I will goe, if so be that the Lord will come and meet me: and whatsoever he sheweth me, I will tell thee: so he went forth alone.
23.4: And God met Balaam, and Balaam sayd unto him, I have prepared seven altars, and have offred upon every altar a bullock and a ramme.
23.5: And the Lord put an answer in Balaams mouth, and sayde, Go again to Balak, and say on this wise.
23.6: So when he returned unto him, loe, hee stood by his burnt offering, he, and all the princes of Moab.
23.7: Then he uttered his parable, and sayde, Balak the king of Moab hath brought mee from Aram out of the mountaines of the East, saying, Come, curse Iaakob for my sake: come, and detest Israel.
23.8: How shall I curse, where God hath not cursed? or how shall I detest, where the Lord hath not detested?
23.9: For from the top of the rocks I did see him, and from the hils I did behold him: lo, the people shall dwell by themselves, and shall not be reckened among the nations.
23.10: Who can tell the dust of Iaakob, and the nomber of the fourth part of Israel? Let me die the death of the righteous, and let my last end be like his.
23.11: Then Balak said unto Balaam, What hast thou done unto mee? I took thee to curse mine enemies, and behold, thou hast blessed them altogether.
23.12: And he answered, and said, Must I not take heed to speak that, which the Lord hath put in my mouth?
23.13: And Balak sayde unto him, Come, I pray thee, with mee unto another place, whence thou mayest see them, and thou shalt see but the utmost part of them, and shalt not see them all: therefore curse them out of that place for my sake.
23.14: And he brought him into Sede-sophim to the top of Pisgah, and built seven altars, and offred a bullock, and a ramme on every altar.
23.15: After, he sayde unto Balak, Stand here by thy burnt offring, and I wil meet the Lord yonder.
23.16: And the Lord met Balaam, and put an answer in his mouth, and sayd, Goe again unto Balak, and say thus.
23.17: And when he came to him, behold, hee stood by his burnt offering, and the princes of Moab with him: so Balak sayde unto him, What hath the Lord sayd?
23.18: And he uttered his parable, and sayde, Rise up, Balak, and hear: hearken unto me, thou sonne of Zippor.
23.19: God is not as man, that he should lie, neither as the sonne of man that he should repent: hath he sayde and shall he not do it? and hath he spoken, and shall he not accomplish it?
23.20: Behold, I have received commandement to bless: for he hath blessed, and I cannot alter it.
23.21: Hee seeth none iniquitie in Iaakob, nor seeth no transgression in Israel: the Lord his God is with him, and the ioyfull shout of a king is among them.
23.22: God brought them out of Egypt: their strength is as an vnicorne.
23.23: For there is no sorcerie in Iaakob, nor soothsaying in Israel: according to this time it shalbe sayde of Iaakob and of Israel, What hath God wrought?
23.24: Behold, the people shall rise up as a lyon, and lift up himself as a yong lyon: hee shall not lye down, till he eat of the pray, and till he drink the blood of the slayne.
23.25: Then Balak sayde unto Balaam, Neither curse, nor bless them at all.
23.26: But Balaam answered, and said unto Balak, Told not I thee, saying, All that the Lord speaketh, that must I do?
23.27: Again Balak sayd unto Balaam, Come, I pray thee, I wil bring thee unto another place, if so be it wil please God, that thou mayest thence curse them for my sake.
23.28: So Balak brought Balaam unto the top of Peor, that looketh toward Ieshmon.
23.29: Then Balaam sayde unto Balak, Make me here seven altars, and prepare me here seven bullocks, and seven rammes.
23.30: And Balak did as Balaam had sayd, and offred a bullock and a ram on every altar.

24.1: When Balaam saw that it pleased the Lord to bless Israel, then he went not, as certain times before, to set divinations, but set his face toward the wilderness.
24.2: And Balaam lift up his eyes, and looked upon Israel, which dwelt according to their tribes, and the Spirit of God came upon him.
24.3: And he uttered his parable, and sayd, Balaam the sonne of Beor hath sayde, and the man, whose eyes were shut up, hath sayd,
24.4: He hath sayde, which heard the wordes of God, and saw the vision of the Almightie, and falling in a traunce had his eyes opened:
24.5: How goodly are thy tentes, O Iaakob, and thine habitations, O Israel!
24.6: As the valleis, are they stretched forth, as gardes by the rivers side, as the aloe trees, which the Lord hath planted, as the cedars beside the waters.
24.7: The water droppeth out of his bucket, and his seed shalbe in many waters, and his king shall be hier then Agag, and his kingdom shall bee exalted.
24.8: God brought him out of Egypt: his strength shalbe as an vnicorne: he shall eat the nations his enemies, and bruise their bones, and shoot them through with his arrowes.
24.9: He coucheth and lieth down as a yong lion, and as a lion: who shall stirre him up? blessed is he that blesseth thee, and cursed is he that curseth thee.
24.10: Then Balak was very angry with Balaam, and smote his handes together: so Balak sayde unto Balaam, I sent for thee to curse mine enemies, and behold, thou hast blessed them now three times.
24.11: Therefore now flee unto thy place: I thought surely to promote thee unto honour, but loe, the Lord hath kept thee back from honour.
24.12: Then Balaam answered Balak, Told I not also thy messengers, which thou sentest unto me, saying,
24.13: If Balak would give me his house ful of silver and gold, I can not pass the commandement of the Lord, to doe either good or bad of mine own mind? what the Lord shall commaund, the same will I speak.
24.14: And now behold, I goe unto my people: come, I will advertise thee what this people shall doe to thy folk in the later dayes.
24.15: And he uttered his parable, and sayd, Balaam the sonne of Beor hath sayde, and the man whose eyes were shut up, hath sayd,
24.16: He hath said that heard the words of God, and hath the knowledge of the most High, and saw the vision of the Almightie, and falling in a traunce had his eyes opened:
24.17: I shall see him, but not now: I shall behold him, but not neere: there shall come a star of Iaakob, and a scepter shall rise of Israel, and shall smite the coastes of Moab, and destroy all the sonnes of Sheth.
24.18: And Edom shalbe possessed, and Seir shall be a possession to their enemies: but Israel shall do valiantly.
24.19: He also that shall have dominion shall bee of Iaakob, and shall destroy the remnant of the citie.
24.20: And when he looked on Amalek, he uttered his parable, and sayd, Amalek was the first of the nations: but his latter end shall come to destruction.
24.21: And he looked on the Kenites, and uttered his parable, and sayde, Strong is thy dwelling place, and put thy nest in the rock.
24.22: Nevertheless, the Kenite shalbe spoyled until Asshur cary thee away captive.
24.23: Again he uttered his parable, and sayd, Alas, who shall live when God doeth this?
24.24: The ships also shall come from the coastes of Chittim, and subdue Asshur, and shall subdue Eber, and he also shall come to destruction.
24.25: Then Balaam rose up, and went and returned to his place: and Balak also went his way.

25.1: Now whiles Israel abode in Shittim, the people began to commit whoredom with the daughters of Moab:
25.2: Which called the people unto the sacrifice of their gods, and the people ate, and bowed down to their gods.
25.3: And Israel coupled himself unto Baal Peor: wherefore the wrath of the Lord was kindled against Israel:
25.4: And the Lord sayde unto Moses, Take all the heades of the people, and hang them up before the Lord against ye sunne, that the indignation of the Lords wrath may be turned from Israel.
25.5: Then Moses sayd unto the Judges of Israel, Every one slay his men that were ioyned unto Baal Peor.
25.6: And behold, one of the children of Israel came and brought unto his brethren a Midianitish woman in the sight of Moses, and in the sight of all the Congregation of the children of Israel, who wept before the door of the Tabernacle of the Congregation.
25.7: And when Phinehas the sonne of Eleazar the sonne of Aaron the Priest saw it, hee rose up from the middes of the Congregation, and took a spear in his hand,
25.8: And followed ye man of Israel into the tent, and thrust them both through: to wit, the man of Israel, and the woman, through her belly: so the plague ceased from the children of Israel.
25.9: And there died in that plague, four and twentie thousand.
25.10: Then the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
25.11: Phinehas the sonne of Eleazar, the sonne of Aaron the Priest, hath turned mine anger away from the children of Israel, while hee was zealous for my sake among them: therefore I have not consumed the children of Israel in my ielousie.
25.12: Wherefore say to him, Behold, I give unto him my covenant of peace,
25.13: And he shall have it, and his seed after him, even the covenant of the priestes office for ever, because he was zealous for his God, and hath made an atonement for the children of Israel.
25.14: And the name of the Israelite thus slayne, which was killed with the Midianitish woman, was Zimri the sonne of Salu, prince of the familie of the Simeonites.
25.15: And the name of the Midianitish woman, that was slayne, was Cozbi the daughter of Zur, who was head over the people of his fathers house in Midian.
25.16: Again ye Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
25.17: Vex the Midianites, and smite them:
25.18: For they trouble you with their wiles, wherewith they have beguiled you as concerning Peor, and as concerning their sister Cozbi ye daughter of a prince of Midian, which was slayne in the day of the plague because of Peor.

26.1: And so after the plague, the Lord spake unto Moses, and to Eleazar the sonne of Aaron the Priest, saying,
26.2: Take the nomber of all the Congregation of the children of Israel from twentie yeere old and above throughout their fathers houses, all that go forth to war in Israel.
26.3: So Moses and Eleazar the Priest spake unto them in the plain of Moab, by Iorden toward Jericho, saying,
26.4: From twentie yeere old and above ye shall nomber the people, as the Lord had commanded Moses, and the childre of Israel, when they came out of the land of Egypt.
26.5: Reuben the first borne of Israel: the children of Reube were: Hanoch, of whom came the familie of the Hanochites, and of Pallu the familie of the Palluites:
26.6: Of Hesron, the familie of the Hesronites: of Carmi, the familie of the Carmites.
26.7: These are the families of the Reubenites: and they were in nomber three and fourtie thousand, seven hundreth and thirtie.
26.8: And the sonnes of Pallu, Eliab:
26.9: And the sonnes of Eliab, Nemuel, and Dathan, and Abiram: this Dathan and Abiram were famous in the Congregation, and strove against Moses and against Aaron in the assemblie of Korah, when they strove against the Lord.
26.10: And the earth opened her mouth, and swalowed them up with Korah, when the Congregation died, what time the fire consumed, two hundreth and fiftie men, who were for a sign.
26.11: Notwithstanding, all the sonnes of Korah dyed not.
26.12: And the children of Simeon after their families were: Nemuel, of whom came the familie of the Nemuelites: of Jamin, the familie of the Jaminites: of Jachin, the familie of the Jachinites:
26.13: Of Zerah, the familie of the Zarhites: of Shaul, the familie of the Shaulites.
26.14: These are the families of the Simeonites: two and twentie thousand and two hundreth.
26.15: The sonnes of Gad after their families were: Zephon, of whom came ye familie of the Zephonites: of Haggi, the familie of the Haggites: of Shuni, the familie of the Shunites:
26.16: Of Ozni, the familie of the Oznites: of Eri, the familie of the Erites:
26.17: Of Arod, the familie of the Arodites: of Areli, the familie of the Arelites.
26.18: These are the families of the sonnes of Gad, according to their nombers, fourtie thousand and five hundreth.
26.19: The sonnes of Judah, Er and Onan: but Er and Onan died in the land of Canaan.
26.20: So were the sonnes of Judah after their families: of Shelah came the familie of ye Shelanites: of Pharez, the familie of the Pharzites, of Zerah, the familie of the Zarhites.
26.21: And the sonnes of Pharez were: of Hesron, the familie of the Hesronites: of Hamul, the familie of the Hamulites.
26.22: These are the families of Judah, after their nombers, seuentie and six thousand and five hundreth.
26.23: The sonnes of Issachar, after their families were: Tola, of whom came the familie of the Tolaites: of Pua, the familie of the Punites:
26.24: Of Jashub the familie of the Jashubites: of Shimron, the familie of the Shimronites.
26.25: These are the families of Issachar, after their nombers, threescore and four thousand and three hundreth.
26.26: The sonnes of Zebulun, after their families were: of Sered, the familie of the Sardites: of Elon, the familie of the Elonites: of Jahleel, the familie of the Jahleelites.
26.27: These are the families of the Zebulunites, after their nombers, three score thousand and five hundreth.
26.28: The sonnes of Joseph, after their families were Manasseh and Ephraim.
26.29: The sonnes of Manasseh were: of Machir, the familie of the Machirites: and Machir begat Gilead: of Gilead came the familie of the Gileadites.
26.30: These are the sonnes of Gilead: of Jezer, the familie of the Jezerites: of Helek, the familie of the Helekites.
26.31: Of Asriel, the familie of the Asrielites: of Shechem, the familie of Shichmites.
26.32: Of Shemida, the familie of the Shemidaites: of Hepher, the familie of the Hepherites.
26.33: And Zelophehad the sonne of Hepher had no sonnes, but daughters: and the names of the daughters of Zelophehad were Mahlah, and Noah, Hoglah, Milcah and Tirzah.
26.34: These are the families of Manasseh, and the nomber of them, two and fiftie thousand and seven hundreth.
26.35: These are the sonnes of Ephraim after their families: of Shuthelah came the familie of the Shuthalhites: of Becher, the familie of the Bachrites: of Tahan, the familie of the Tahanites.
26.36: And these are the sonnes of Shuthelah: of Eran the familie of the Eranites.
26.37: These are the families of the sonnes of Ephraim after their nombers, two and thirtie thousand and five hundreth. these are the sonnes of Joseph after their families.
26.38: These are the sonnes of Beniamin after their families: of Bela came the familie of the Belaites: of Ashbel, the familie of the Ashbelites: of Ahiram, the familie of the Ahiramites:
26.39: Of Shupham, the familie of the Suphamites: of Hupham, the familie of the Huphamites.
26.40: And the sonnes of Bela were Ard and Naaman: of Ard came the familie of the Ardites, of Naaman, the familie of the Naamites.
26.41: These are the sonnes of Beniamin after their families, and their nombers, five and fourtie thousand and six hundreth.
26.42: These are the sonnes of Dan after their families: of Shuham came the familie of the Shuhamites: these are the families of Dan after their housholdes.
26.43: All the families of the Shuhamites were after their nombers, threescore and four thousand, and four hundreth.
26.44: The sonnes of Asher after their families were: of Jimnah, the familie of the Jimnites: of Isui, the familie of the Isuites: of Beriah, the familie of the Berijtes.
26.45: The sonnes of Beriah were, of Heber the familie of the Heberites: of Malchiel, the familie of the Malchielites.
26.46: And the name of the daughter of Asher was Sarah.
26.47: These are the families of the sonnes of Asher after their nombers, three and fifty thousand and four hundreth.
26.48: The sonnes of Naphtali, after their families were: of Jahzeel, the families of the Jahzeelites: of Guni, the familie of the Gunites.
26.49: Of Jezer, the familie of the Izrites: of Shillem, the familie of the Shillemites.
26.50: These are the families of Naphtali according to their housholdes, and their nomber, five and fourtie thousand and four hundreth.
26.51: These are the nombers of the children of Israel: six hundreth and one thousand, seven hundreth and thirtie.
26.52: And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
26.53: Unto these the land shalbe deuided for an inheritance, according to the nomber of names.
26.54: To many thou shalt give the more inheritance, and to few thou shalt give less inheritance: to every one according to his nomber shalbe given his inheritance.
26.55: Notwithstanding, the land shalbe deuided by lot: according to the names of the tribes of their fathers they shall inherit:
26.56: According to the lot shall the possession thereof be deuided between many and few.
26.57: These also are the nobers of ye Levites, after their families: of Gershon came ye familie of the Gershonites: of Kohath, ye familie of the Kohathites: of Merari, the familie of the Merarites.
26.58: These are the families of Levi, the familie of the Libnites: the familie of the Hebronites: the familie of the Mahlites: the familie of the Mushites: the familie of the Korhites: and Kohath begat Amram.
26.59: And Amrams wife was called Jochebed the daughter of Levi, which was borne unto Levi in Egypt: and she bare unto Amram Aaron, and Moses, and Miriam their sister.
26.60: And unto Aaron were borne Nadab, and Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
26.61: And Nadab and Abihu dyed, because they offred strange fire before the Lord.
26.62: And their nombers were three and twentie thousand, all males from a moneth old and above: for they were not nombred among the children of Israel, because there was none inheritance given them among the children of Israel.
26.63: These are the nombers of Moses and Eleazar the Priest which nombred the children of Israel in the plain of Moab, neere Iorden, toward Jericho.
26.64: And among these there was not a man of them, whom Moses and Aaron the Priest nobred, when they told the children of Israel in the wildernes of Sinai.
26.65: For the Lord said of them, They shall die in the wildernes: so there was not left a man of them, save Caleb the sonne of Jephunneh, and Joshua the sonne of Nun.

27.1: Then came the daughters of Zelophehad, the sonne of Hepher, the sonne of Gilead, the sonne of Machir, the sonne of Manasseh, of the familie of Manasseh, the sonne of Joseph (and the names of his daughters were these, Mahlah, Noah and Hoglah, and Milcah, and Tirzah)
27.2: And stood before Moses, and before Eleazar the Priest, and before the Princes, and all the assemblie, at the door of the Tabernacle of the Congregation, saying,
27.3: Our father dyed in the wildernes, and he was not among the assemblie of them that were assembled against the Lord in the companie of Korah, but died in his sinne, and had no sonnes.
27.4: Wherefore should the name of our father be taken away from among his familie, because he hath no sonne? give us a possession among the brethren of our father.
27.5: Then Moses brought their cause before the Lord.
27.6: And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
27.7: The daughters of Zelophehad speak right: thou shalt give them a possession to inherit among their fathers brethren, and shalt turn the inheritance of their father unto them.
27.8: Also thou shalt speak unto the children of Israel, saying, If a man die and have no sonne, then ye shall turn his inheritaunce unto his daughter.
27.9: And if he have no daughter, ye shall give his inheritance unto his brethren.
27.10: And if he have no brethren, ye shall give his inheritance unto his fathers brethren.
27.11: And if his father have no brethren, ye shall give his inheritance unto his next kinsman of his familie, and he shall possess it: and this shall be unto the children of Israel a law of iudgement, as the Lord hath commanded Moses.
27.12: Again the Lord said unto Moses, Go up into this mount of Abarim, and behold ye land which I have given unto the children of Israel.
27.13: And when thou hast seen it, thou shalt be gathered unto thy people also, as Aaron thy brother was gathered.
27.14: For ye were disobedient unto my word in the desert of Zin, in the strife of the assemblie, to sanctifie me in the waters before their eyes. That is the water of Meribah in Kadesh in the wilderness of Zin.
27.15: Then Moses spake unto the Lord, saying,
27.16: Let the Lord God of the spirits of all flesh appoint a man over the Congregation,
27.17: Who may goe out and in before them, and lead them out and in, that the Congregation of the Lord be not as sheep, which have not a shepheard.
27.18: And the Lord said unto Moses, Take thee Joshua the sonne of Nun, in whom is the Spirit, and put thine handes upon him,
27.19: And set him before Eleazar the Priest, and before all the Congregation, and give him a charge in their sight.
27.20: And give him of thy glory, that all the Congregation of ye children of Israel may obey.
27.21: And he shall stand before Eleazar the Priest, who shall ask counsel for him by the iudgement of Urim before the Lord: at his word they shall goe out, and at his word they shall come in, both he, and all the children of Israel with him and all the Congregation.
27.22: So Moses did as the Lord had commanded him, and he took Joshua, and set him before Eleazar the Priest, and before all the Congregation.
27.23: Then he put his handes upon him, and gave him a charge, as the Lord had spoken by the hand of Moses.

28.1: And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
28.2: Command the children of Israel, and say unto them, Ye shall observe to offer unto me in their due season mine offering, and my bread, for my sacrifices made by fire for a sweet sauour unto me.
28.3: Also thou shalt say unto them, This is the offring made by fire which ye shall offer unto the Lord, two lambes of a yeere old without spot, daily, for a continual burnt offring.
28.4: One lamb shalt thou prepare in the morning, and the other lamb shalt thou prepare at even.
28.5: And the tenth part of an Ephah of fine flour for a meat offering mingled with the fourth part of an Hin of beaten oyle.
28.6: This shalbe a daily burnt offering, as was made in the mount Sinai for a sweet sauour: it is a sacrifice made by fire unto the Lord.
28.7: And the drink offring thereof the fourth part of an Hin for one lamb: in the holy place cause to powre the drink offring unto the Lord.
28.8: And the other lamb thou shalt prepare at even: as the meat offring of the morning, and as the drink offering thereof shalt thou prepare this for an offring made by fire of sweet sauour unto the Lord.
28.9: But on the Sabbath day ye shall offer two lambes of a yere old, without spot, and two tenth deales of fine flour for a meat offring mingled with oyle, and the drink offring thereof.
28.10: This is ye burnt offring of every Sabbath, beside the continual burnt offring, and drink offring thereof.
28.11: And in the beginning of your moneths, ye shall offer a burnt offring unto the Lord, two yong bullockes, and a ramme, and seven lambes of a yeere old, without spot,
28.12: And three tenth deales of fine flour for a meat offring mingled with oyle for one bullock, and two tenth deales of fine flour for a meat offring, mingled with oyle for one ramme,
28.13: And a tenth deal of fine flour mingled with oyle for a meat offring unto one lamb: for a burnt offring of sweet sauour: it is an offring made by fire unto the Lord.
28.14: And their drink offrings shalbe half an Hin of wine unto one bullock, and the third part of an Hin unto a ram, and ye fourth part of an Hin unto a labe: this is the burnt offring of every moneth, throughout the moneths of the yeere.
28.15: And one hee goat for a sinne offring unto the Lord shalbe prepared, besides the continual burnt offring, and his drink offring.
28.16: Also the fourtenth day of the first moneth is the Passeouer of the Lord.
28.17: And in ye fiftenth day of the same moneth is the feast: seven dayes shall vnleauened bread be eaten.
28.18: In the first day shalbe an holy convocation, ye shall do no servile work therein.
28.19: But ye shall offer a sacrifice made by fire for a burnt offring unto the Lord, two yong bullocks, one ram, and seven lambes of a yeere old: see that they be without blemish.
28.20: And their meat offering shalbe of fine flour mingled with oyle: three tenth deales shall ye prepare for a bullock, and two tenth deales for a ramme:
28.21: One tenth deal shalt thou prepare for every lamb, even for the seven lambes.
28.22: And an hee goat for a sinne offering, to make an atonement for you.
28.23: Ye shall prepare these, beside the burnt offering in the morning, which is a continual burnt sacrifice.
28.24: After this maner ye shall prepare throughout all the seven dayes, for the mainteining of the offring made by fire for a sweet sauour unto the Lord: it shall be done beside the continual burnt offring and drink offring thereof.
28.25: And in ye seventh day ye shall have an holy convocation, wherein ye shall do no servile work.
28.26: Also in the day of your first fruits, when ye bring a new meat offring unto the Lord, according to your weekes ye shall have an holy convocation, and ye shall do no servile work in it:
28.27: But ye shall offer a burnt offering for a sweet sauour unto the Lord, two yong bullocks, a ramme, and seven lambes of a yeere old,
28.28: And their meat offring of fine flour mingled with oyle, three tenth deales unto a bullock, two tenth deales to a ram,
28.29: And one tenth deal unto every lamb throughout the seven lambes,
28.30: And an hee goat to make an atonement for you:
28.31: (Ye shall doe this besides the continual burnt offring, and his meat offring:) see they be without blemish, with their drink offrings.

29.1: Moreover, in the first day of the seventh moneth ye shall have an holy convocation: ye shall doe no servile work therein: it shall be a day of blowing the trumpets unto you.
29.2: And ye shall make a burnt offering for a sweet sauour unto the Lord: one yong bullock, one ram, and seven lambes of a yeere old, without blemish.
29.3: And their meat offring shalbe of fine flour mingled with oyle, three tenth deales unto the bullock, and two tenth deales unto the ramme,
29.4: And one tenth deal unto one lamb, for the seven lambes,
29.5: And an hee goat for a sinne offering to make an atonement for you,
29.6: Beside the burnt offring of the moneth, and his meat offring, and the continual burnt offring, and his meat offring and the drink offrings of the same, according to their maner, for a sweet sauour: it is a sacrifice made by fire unto ye Lord.
29.7: And ye shall have in ye tenth day of the seventh moneth, an holy convocation: and ye shall humble your soules, and shall not doe any work therein:
29.8: But ye shall offer a burnt offring unto the Lord for a sweet sauour: one yong bullock, a ramme, and seven lambes of a yeere old: see they be without blemish.
29.9: And their meat offering shall be of fine flour mingled with oyle, three tenth deales to a bullock, and two tenth deales to a ramme,
29.10: One tenth deal unto every lamb, thoroughout the seven lambes,
29.11: An hee goat for a sinne offring, (beside ye sinne offring to make the atonement and the continual burnt offring and the meat offring thereof) and their drink offrings.
29.12: And in the fifteenth day of the seventh moneth ye shall have an holie convocation: ye shall do no servile work therein, but yee shall keep a feast unto the Lord seven daies.
29.13: And ye shall offer a burnt offring for a sacrifice made by fire of sweet sauour unto the Lord, thirteen yong bullockes, two rammes, and fourtene lambes of a yeere old: they shall bee without blemish.
29.14: And their meat offering shall bee of fine flour mingled with oyle, three tenth deales unto every bullock of the thirteen bullockes, two tenth deales to either of the two rammes,
29.15: And one tenth deal unto eche of ye fourteen lambes,
29.16: And one hee goat for a sinne offring, beside the continual burnt offring, his meat offring, and his drink offring.
29.17: And the second day ye shall offer twelve yong bullockes, two rams, fourteen lambes of a yeere old without blemish,
29.18: With their meat offring and their drink offrings for the bullockes, for the rammes, and for the lambes according to their nomber, after the maner,
29.19: And an hee goat for a sinne offring, (beside the continual burnt offering and his meat offring) and their drink offrings.
29.20: Also the third day ye shall offer eleven bullocks, two rams, and fourteen lambes of a yeere old without blemish,
29.21: With their meat offring and their drink offrings, for the bullockes, for the rams, and for the lambes, after their nomber according to the maner,
29.22: And an hee goat for a sinne offring, beside the continual burnt offring, and his meat offring and his drink offring.
29.23: And the fourth day ye shall offer tenne bullocks, two rammes, and fourteen lambes of a yeere old without blemish.
29.24: Their meat offring and their drink offrings, for the bullockes, for the rammes, and for the lambes according to their nomber, after the maner,
29.25: And an hee goat for a sinne offering beside the continual burnt offring, his meat offering and his drink offering.
29.26: In the fifth day also ye shall offer nine bullockes, two rammes, and fourteen lambes of a yeere old without blemish,
29.27: And their meat offering and their drink offrings for the bullockes, for the rammes, and for the lambes according to their nomber, after the maner,
29.28: And an hee goat for a sinne offring, beside the continual burnt offring, and his meat offring and his drink offering.
29.29: And in the sixt day ye shall offer eight bullockes, two rams, and fourteen lambes of a yeere old without blemish,
29.30: And their meat offring, and their drink offrings for the bullockes, for the rammes, and for the lambes according to their nomber, after the maner,
29.31: And an hee goat for a sinne offring, beside the continual burnt offring, his meat offring and his drink offrings.
29.32: In the seventh day also ye shall offer seven bullocks, two rammes and fourteen lambes of a yeere old without blemish,
29.33: And their meat offering and their drink offrings for the bullockes, for the rammes, and for the lambes according to their nomber, after their maner,
29.34: And an hee goat for a sinne offring, beside the continual burnt offring, his meat offering and his drink offring.
29.35: In the eight day, yee shall have a solemn assemblie: yee shall doe no servile work therein,
29.36: But yee shall offer a burnt offering, a sacrifice made by fire for a sweet sauour unto the Lord, one bullock, one ram, and seven lambes of a yeere old without blemish,
29.37: Their meat offring and their drink offrings for the bullock, for the ramme, and for the lambes according to their nomber, after the maner,
29.38: And an hee goat for a sinne offring, beside the continual burnt offring, and his meat offring, and his drink offring.
29.39: These things ye shall do unto the Lord in your feastes, beside your vowes, and your free offrings, for your burnt offrings, and for your meat offrings, and for your drink offrings and for your peace offrings.

30.1: Then Moses spake unto the children of Israel according to all that the Lord had commanded him,
30.2: Moses also spake unto the heads of ye tribes concerning the children of Israel, saying, This is the thing which the Lord hath commanded,
30.3: Whosoever voweth a vow unto the Lord, or sweareth an othe to bind him self by a bond, he shall not break his promise, but shall do according to al that proceedeth out of his mouth.
30.4: If a woman also vow a vow unto the Lord, and bind her self by a bond, being in her fathers house, in the time of her youth,
30.5: And her father hear her vow and bond, wherewith she hath bound her self, and her father hold his peace concerning her, then all her vowes shall stand, and every bond, wherewith she hath bound her self, shall stand.
30.6: But if her father disallow her the same day that he heareth all her vowes and bondes, wherewith she hath bound her self, they shall not bee of value, and the Lord will forgive her, because her father disallowed her.
30.7: And if she have an husband when she voweth or pronounceth ought with her lips, wherewith she bindeth her self,
30.8: If her husband heard it, and holdeth his peace concerning her, the same day he heareth it, then her vow shall stand, and her bondes wherewith she bindeth her self shall stand in effect.
30.9: But if her husband disallow her the same day that hee heareth it, then shall hee make her vow which she hath made, and that that she hath pronounced with her lips, wherewith she bound her self, of none effect: and the Lord will forgive her.
30.10: But every vow of a widow, and of her that is divorced (wherewith she hath bound her self) shall stand in effect with her.
30.11: And if she vowed in her husbands house, or bound her self streightly with an othe,
30.12: And her husband hath heard it, and held his peace cocerning her, not disalowing her, then all her vowes shall stand, and every bond, wherewith she bound her self, shall stand in effect.
30.13: But if her husband disanulled them, the same day that he heard them, nothing that proceeded out of her lippes concerning her vowes or concerning her bondes, shall stand in effect: for her husband hath disanulled them: and the Lord will forgive her.
30.14: So every vow, and every othe or bond, made to humble the soul, her husband may stablish it, or her husband may break it.
30.15: But if her husband hold his peace concerning her from day to day, then he stablisheth al her vowes and all her bondes which she hath made: hee hath confirmed them because he held his peace concerning her the same day that hee heard them.
30.16: But if he break them after that he hath heard them, then shall he bear her iniquitie.
30.17: These are the ordinances which the Lord commanded Moses, between a man and his wife, and between the father and his daughter, being young in her fathers house.

31.1: And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
31.2: Revenge the children of Israel of the Midianites, and afterward shalt thou be gathered unto thy people.
31.3: And Moses spake to the people, saying, Harness some of you unto war, and let them goe against Midian, to execute the vengeance of the Lord against Midian.
31.4: A thousand of every tribe throughout all the tribes of Israel, shall ye send to the war.
31.5: So there were taken out of the thousands of Israel, twelve thousand prepared unto war, of every tribe a thousand.
31.6: And Moses sent them to the war, even a thousand of every tribe, and sent them with Phinehas the sonne of Eleazar the Priest to the war: and the holy instruments, that is, the trumpets to blow were in his hand.
31.7: And they warred against Midian, as the Lord had commanded Moses, and slue all the males.
31.8: They slue also the Kings of Midian among them that were slain: Evi and Rekem, and Zur, and Hur and Reba five kings of Midian, and they slue Balaam the sonne of Beor with the sword:
31.9: But the children of Israel took the women of Midian prisoners, and their children, and spoyled all their cattell, and all their flockes, and all their goods.
31.10: And they burnt all their cities, wherein they dwelt, and all their villages with fire.
31.11: And they took all the spoyle and all the pray both of men and beastes.
31.12: And they brought the captives and that which they had taken, and the spoyle unto Moses and to Eleazar the Priest, and unto the Congregation of the children of Israel, into ye camp in the playne of Moab, which was by Iorden toward Jericho.
31.13: Then Moses and Eleazar the Priest, and all the princes of the Congregation went out of the camp to meet them.
31.14: And Moses was angry with the captaines of the host, with the captaines over thousands, and captaines over hundreds, which came from the war and battel.
31.15: And Moses sayde unto them, What? have ye saved all the women?
31.16: Behold, these caused the children of Israel through the counsel of Balaam to commit a trespass against the Lord, as concerning Peor, and there came a plague among the Congregation of the Lord.
31.17: Now therefore, slay all the males among the children, and kill all the women that have knowen man by carnal copulation.
31.18: But all the women children that have not knowen carnal copulation, keep alive for your selves.
31.19: And ye shall remain without the host seven dayes, all that have killed any person, and all that have touched any dead, and purifie both your selves and your prisoners the third day and the seventh.
31.20: Also ye shall purifie every garment and all that is made of skins and al work of goates hear, and all things made of wood.
31.21: And Eleazar ye Priest sayd unto the men of war, which went to the battel, This is the ordinance of the law which the Lord commanded Moses,
31.22: As for gold, and silver, brass, yron, tynne, and lead:
31.23: Even all that may abide the fire, yee shall make it goe through the fire, and it shalbe clean: yet, it shalbe purified with the water of purification: and all that suffereth not the fire, yee shall cause to pass by the water.
31.24: Ye shall wash also your clothes the seventh day, and ye shalbe clean: and afterward ye shall come into the Host.
31.25: And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
31.26: Take the summe of the praie that was taken, both of persons and of cattell, thou and Eleazar the Priest, and the chief fathers of the Congregation.
31.27: And deuide the pray between the souldiers that went to the war, and all the Congregation.
31.28: And thou shalt take a tribute unto ye Lord of the men of war, which went out to battel: one person of five hundreth, both of the persons, and of the beeves, and of the asses, and of the sheep.
31.29: Yee shall take it of their half and give it unto Eleazar the Priest, as an heave offring of the Lord.
31.30: But of the half of the children of Israel thou shalt take one, taken out of fiftie, both of the persons, of the beeves, of the asses, and of the sheep, even of all the cattel: and thou shalt give them unto the Levites, which have the charge of the Tabernacle of the Lord.
31.31: And Moses and Eleazar the priest did as the Lord had commanded Moses.
31.32: And the bootie, to wit, the rest of the praie which the men of war had spoyled, was six hundreth seuentie and five thousand sheep,
31.33: And seuentie and two thousand beeves,
31.34: And three score and one thousand asses,
31.35: And two and thirtie thousand persons in all, of women that had lyen by no man.
31.36: And the half, to wit, the part of them that went out to war touching the nomber of sheep, was three hundreth seven and thirtie thousand, and five hundreth.
31.37: And the Lordes tribute of the sheep was six hundreth and seuentie and five:
31.38: And the beeves were six and thirty thousad, whereof the Lordes tribute was seuentie and two.
31.39: And the asses were thirtie thousand and five hundreth, whereof the Lordes tribute was three score and one:
31.40: And of persons sixtene thousand, whereof the Lordes tribute was two and thirtie persons.
31.41: And Moses gave the tribute of the Lordes offring unto Eleazar the Priest, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
31.42: And of the half of the children of Israel, which Moses deuided from the men of war,
31.43: (For the half that perteined unto the Congregation, was three hundreth thirtie and seven thousand sheep and five hundreth,
31.44: And six and thirtie thousand beeves,
31.45: And thirtie thousand asses, and five hudreth,
31.47: Moses, I say, took of the half that perteined unto the children of Israel, one taken out of fiftie, both of the persons, and of the cattell, and gave them unto the Levites, which have the charge of the Tabernacle of the Lord, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
31.48: Then the captaines which were over thousandes of the host, the captaines over the thousandes, and the captaines over the hundreds came unto Moses:
31.49: And said to Moses, Thy servants have taken the summe of the men of war which are under our authoritie, and there lacketh not one man of us.
31.50: We have therefore brought a present unto the Lord, what every man found of jewels of gold, bracelets, and cheines, rings, ear ringes, and ornaments of the legges, to make an atonement for our soules before the Lord.
31.51: And Moses and Eleazar the Priest took the gold of them, and all wrought jewels,
31.52: And all the gold of the offring that they offered up to the Lord (of the captaines over thousands and hundreds) was sixteen thousand seven hundreth and fiftie shekels,
31.53: (For the men of war had spoyled, every man for him self)
31.54: And Moses and Eleazar the Priest took the gold of the captaines over the thousandes, and over the hundreds, and brought it into the Tabernacle of the Congregation, for a memorial of the children of Israel before the Lord.

32.1: Now the children of Reuben, and the children of Gad had an exceeding great multitude of cattell: and they saw the land of Jazer, and the land of Gilead, that it was an apt place for cattel.
32.2: Then the children of Gad, and the childre of Reuben came, and spake unto Moses and to Eleazar the Priest, and unto the princes of the Congregation, saying,
32.3: The land of Ataroth, and Dibon, and Jazer, and Nimrah, and Heshbon, and Elealeh, and Shebam, and Nebo, and Beon,
32.4: Which countrey the Lord smote before the Congregation of Israel, is a land meet for cattell, and thy servants have cattell:
32.5: Wherefore, said they, if we have foud grace in thy sight, let this land be given unto thy servants for a possession, and bring us not over Iorde.
32.6: And Moses said unto the children of Gad, and to the children of Reuben, Shall your brethren goe to war, and ye tary heere?
32.7: Wherefore now discourage ye the heart of the children of Israel, to goe over into the land, which the Lord hath given them?
32.8: Thus did your fathers when I sent them from Kadesh-barnea to see the land.
32.9: For when they went up even unto the river of Eshcol, and saw the land: they discouraged the heart of the childre of Israel, that they would not goe into the land, which the Lord had given them.
32.10: And the Lordes wrath was kindled the same day, and he did swear, saying,
32.11: None of the men that came out of Egypt from twentie yeere old and above, shall see the land for the which I sware unto Abraham, to Izhak, and to Iaakob, because they have not wholly followed me:
